## Dear Christian Reader!

For several years now, it has been noted with pleasure that in many places the blessed book, *The Way to Christ* <note>original: *Weg zu Christo*</note>, was being sought after. Since it was no longer available anywhere, there was a great desire to satisfy the hunger of these good souls and offer them, by means of a new edition <term>Auflage|A specific printing or version of a published work</term>, a pure, powerful food sanctified by God Himself; which would at the same time serve them as an unerring guide

When a person wishes to proceed to repentance <note>original: *Busse*, which implies both an internal change of heart and the active practice of penitence</note> and turn to GOD with their prayer, they should, before all prayer, examine their mind <term>mind: *Gemüth*, the deep seat of the soul’s will, emotions, and consciousness</term>, how it stands so completely turned away from GOD; how it has become unfaithful to GOD; how it is directed only toward the temporal, fragile, earthly life, and carries no true love toward GOD and one's neighbor; and how it thus lusts and seethes entirely against GOD’s commandment, seeking only itself in temporal, transitory fleshly lust.

2. Secondly, he should consider how all of this is an enmity against God, which Satan, through his deceit, awakened in our first parents <note>referring to Adam and Eve</note>; for the sake of which abomination we must die the death and rot with our bodies.

3. Thirdly, he should consider the three cruel chains to which our soul is firmly bound during the time of this earthly life: The first is GOD’s strict wrath, the abyss and dark world, which is the center and natural life of the soul. The other chain is the devil's desire toward the soul, with which he constantly sifts and tempts the soul, and without ceasing wishes to plunge it from GOD’s truth into vanity—such as pride, greed, envy, and wrath—and constantly inflames and kindles those same evil qualities in the soul with his desire, whereby the soul's will turns away from God and enters into a selfhood <term>selfhood: *Selbheit*, a state of being centered on the ego rather than on God</term>. The third and most harmful chain, to which the poor soul stands bound, is the corrupted and entirely vain, earthly, mortal flesh and blood, full of evil desire and inclination. 5. 6. 9. In such contemplation, a person will feel in his heart and mind—especially if he constantly keeps his end <note>The "end" refers to one’s death and the subsequent judgment.</note> before him—that he will gain a heartfelt longing and desire for **God’s** mercy. He will begin to regret his committed sins, seeing that he has spent his days so poorly and has neither noticed nor considered how he stands here in this world like a field in growth, producing fruit either in **God’s** love or His wrath. He will first realize that he has not yet worked at all in Christ's vineyard, and that he is a dry branch on the vine of Christ <note>A reference to John 15:1-6, where branches that do not bear fruit are cut off and withered.</note>. Then, in many whom the Spirit of Christ touches in such contemplation, a great misery and heartache—a lamenting within themselves—begins overwhelmingly over the days of their wickedness, which they have thus postponed and spent in vanity without any effect in Christ’s vineyard.

10. Now, for the person whom the Spirit of Christ leads into such contrition, where his heart is opened so that he can recognize and regret his sin, advice is very easy to give: He need only take up the promises of Christ—that **God** does not desire the death of the poor sinner (Ezekiel 33:11), but bids them all to come to Him, and He will refresh them (Matthew 11:28). And that there is great joy in heaven over one sinner who repents (Luke 15:7). Let such a person merely grasp the words of Christ and wrap himself in Christ’s suffering and death.

11. But I wish to speak with those who indeed feel a desire for repentance within themselves, yet can never arrive at a true recognition or right contrition over their committed sins; where the flesh always speaks to the soul: "Wait a while, tomorrow is soon enough." And when tomorrow comes, the flesh speaks again: "Tomorrow." Meanwhile, the poor soul groans and remains in a faint, receiving neither true repentance for the committed sin nor any comfort. To those, I say, I will write out a <term>process</term> <note>original: *Proceß*; here meaning a spiritual method or a path of practice.</note> that I myself have walked—what must be done and how it went for me—so that if anyone should desire to follow it, he will experience what is written hereafter.

...finds such contemplation within himself, that he would gladly repent, yet finds no true remorse for the sins committed in himself, and yet nonetheless feels a hunger for remorse (as the poor imprisoned soul always groans, fears, and must admit its guilt before **God’s** judgment of sins), such a person cannot do better than to gather all his senses, mind, and reason into one. # I. On True Repentance

...drink the water of eternal life from the sweet fountain of **Jesus Christ**, according to **Christ’s** promise and His truly powerful assurance (John 4:10).

15. He should also completely <term>internalize <note>German: *einbilden*. In this context, it does not mean to imagine something false, but to deeply impress a truth upon the soul through meditative focus until it takes shape within the believer.</note></term> the great love of **God**: that **God** does not desire the death of the sinner, but rather wills that he turn back and live (Ezekiel 33:11). He should consider how **Christ** so kindly calls poor sinners to Himself, desiring to refresh them (Matthew 11:28). And he should remember that **God** sent His Son into the world to seek and to save that which is lost—namely, the poor, repentant, returning sinner—and how He gave His life unto death for the sake of the poor sinner, dying for him in our assumed humanity.

16. Furthermore, he should firmly fix in his mind that **God**, in **Christ Jesus**, wants to hear him and receive him into grace far more than he even wants to come to Him. He must believe that in the love of **Christ**, and in the precious name of **Jesus**, **God** can will nothing evil; there is no "look of wrath" in this name. Instead, He is the highest and deepest love and faithfulness, the greatest sweetness of the Godhead in the great name <term>Jehovah <note>Original: *JEHOVA*. This refers to the Tetragrammaton, the sacred name of God, which the author views here as the root of divine sweetness and love revealed through the incarnation.</note></term>. He has revealed this name in our corrupted and <term>faded humanity <note>The "heavenly part" of humanity was believed by some mystical thinkers to have "faded" or become dormant after the Fall of Adam. Salvation is the process of this divine image being re-awakened or "re-colored" by God's grace.</note></term>—that heavenly part which faded in Paradise through sin. God was moved in His heart to instill His sweet love within us, so that the Father’s wrath, which was kindled in us, might be extinguished and transformed into love. All of this was done for the sake of the poor sinner, so that he might once again find an open **Gate of Grace**.

# The First Booklet.

21. To the dear reader who is set upon a **Christian resolution**, I will not hide how it typically goes in such a difficult undertaking—though it happens differently for one than for another, depending on how earnest and great the resolution is. For the **Spirit of God** is unbound and tends to follow many different processes, as He knows each person. However, one who has been in the war can speak of the battle; should it go this way for anyone else, let this serve as a report.

22. It happens that such a heart comes before **God** with a strict resolution and enters into <term>repentance <note>German: *Busse*. This term encompasses both the inner change of heart and the outward act of penance or turning away from sin.</note></term>; but it goes for him as it did for the <note>original: "Cananäischen Weiblein"</note> **Canaanite woman**, as if **God** would not hear. His heart remains without comfort, and his sins and unworthiness still appear before his eyes as if he were not worthy. His mind feels as if it were mute, the soul groans in the depths, and the heart receives nothing; he may find he cannot even pour out his confession before God, just as if his heart and soul were locked shut. The soul would like to, but the flesh holds her captive; the devil covers it up tightly and models the way of <term>vanity <note>As noted previously, "vanity" refers to the hollow and fleeting nature of the material world.</note></term> before him again, tickling him with fleshly lusts, and saying in his mind: "Wait a while; first do this and that, gather money first so that you do not need the world, and then enter into a godly life and into repentance; there is time enough."

23. Oh, how many hundreds perish in such a beginning, when they return again into vanity! It happens to them as to a young <term>graft <note>German: *Pfröpflein*. A metaphor for a young soul recently "grafted" into the spiritual life of Christ, which is still fragile and easily damaged.</note></term> that is broken off by the winds or withered by the heat.

24. Hear, dear soul: if you wish to become a **Knight of death and hell** in your Savior **Christ**, and wish for your young graft to become a tree and grow in the **Kingdom of Christ**, then you must remain standing in your first earnest resolution. It will cost you your first **Fatherly heritage** <note>This likely refers to the worldly life and the "old Adam" inherited through human nature, which must be sacrificed for spiritual rebirth.</note>, along with your body and soul; you will be either an angel in **God** or a devil in hell. If you wish to be crowned, you must fight; you must conquer in **Christ** and not lie defeated beneath the devil. Your resolution must remain standing; you must not prefer temporary honor and goods over this.

25. When the spirit of the flesh says: "Wait a while, it is not pleasant right now," the soul must say: "Now is my time and hour, that I may enter again into my **homeland**."

### The First Little Book

O deep love in the most sweet name of **Jesus**! Yield yourself into my soul’s **desire** <term>desire: original "Begierde." In this mystical context, desire is the "hunger" or magnetic force of the soul that draws the divine into itself.</term>. For you have moved within humanity and revealed yourself according to your great sweetness; you call us to you, we who are hungry and thirsty for you, and you have promised us that you would refresh us. Now, O most holy and sweetest Truth, I open the palate of my soul to you. And though I am unworthy to desire such things from your holiness, I come to you through your bitter suffering and death, for you have sprinkled my impurity with your blood and sanctified me in your humanity. Through your death, you have made an open gate for me to your sweet love in your blood. Through your **holy five wounds** <note>The "Five Wounds" (hands, feet, and side) were a central focus of late medieval and early modern devotion, seen as "fountains" of grace or "gates" through which the soul enters Christ's heart.</note>, from which you shed your blood, I lead my soul’s desire into your love. 

O **Jesus Christ**, Son of God and Man! Take your hard-won inheritance, which your Father has given to you, into yourself. I call out within myself, through your holy blood and death, into you; open yourself within me, so that the spirit of my soul may reach you within itself. Reach out with your thirst toward my thirst within me. Lead your thirst—which you held for us humans on the holy Cross—into my thirst, and quench me with your blood. Do this so that the death within me, which holds me captive, may be drowned in your blood of love, and so that my **faded image** <note>original: "verblichenes Bild." This refers to the *Imago Dei* (Image of God). Böhme believed that when Adam sinned, the radiant, heavenly "body" or image of the soul lost its light and became "pale" or "faded" into the dark, earthly world.</note> (which faded in my father Adam amid the sins of the Kingdom of Heaven) may become alive in your powerful blood. Clothe my soul with it once more as a **new body** that dwells in heaven. Within this body lives your holy power and the Word that became human; it is the temple of your Holy Spirit, who dwells in us, as you have promised us: *We will come to you and make our home within you.*

### Warning to the Reader.

31. Out of good intentions, dear reader, I will not hide from you what has been earnestly shown to me regarding this: If you are still comfortable in the **vanity of the flesh** <note>vanity of the flesh: the state of being preoccupied with worldly, temporary pleasures rather than spiritual growth.</note>, and are not in earnest purpose on the way to the **new rebirth**, intending to become a different person, then leave the words described above in this prayer unspoken. Otherwise, they will become a judgment of God within you. You shall not misuse the holy names of God; be faithfully warned. They belong to the needy soul; if she is truly in earnest, she will experience what they are.

32. Dear soul, there must be earnestness without ceasing. You may well obtain the love of a kiss from the **noble Sophia** <note>Sophia: Representing Divine Wisdom, Sophia is often depicted in mystical literature as the "bride" of the soul, guiding the seeker back to God.</note> in the holy name of **Jesus**; for even without this, she stands before the soul’s door and knocks, warning the sinner of his godless way. If he then desires her love even once, she is willing to help him, and kisses him with the rays of her sweet love, from which the heart receives joy. However, she does not immediately lie down in the **marriage bed** <note>marriage bed: A traditional mystical metaphor for the highest state of union ("unio mystica") between the soul and the Divine.</note> with the soul; that is, she does not quickly awaken within the soul the faded **Heavenly Image**—which faded in Paradise—for there is danger in humanity. Since **Adam** and **Lucifer** fell, it could still easily happen while a person stands so strongly bound in vanity.

33. There must be a faithful bond of your promise if she is to crown you. You must first be tested; she withdraws her rays of love from you again and watches to see if you will keep your faith. 34. Christ was tempted in the wilderness; if you wish to put Him on, you must go through His entire *process* <term>process: original "Proceß." In Böhme’s mysticism, this refers to the "imitation of Christ" not just as a moral example, but as a literal spiritual path where the soul re-experiences Christ's birth, death, and resurrection.</term>, from His incarnation through to His ascension. Even though you cannot nor are required to do exactly what He did, you must nonetheless enter completely into His *process* and continually die to the soul’s vanity within that *process*. For the Virgin *Sophia* <note>Sophia: Divine Wisdom, viewed here as the spiritual bride who restores the soul to its original heavenly state.</note> marries herself to the soul in no other way than through this quality, which blossoms forth in the soul through *Christ’s* death as a new growth that stands in heaven. The earthly body does not grasp her during this time, for it must first die to vanity; but the heavenly image, which faded in *Adam*—as the true seed of the woman in which **God** became human and into which He led His living seed of heavenly essence—that image grasps the noble pearl, in the same manner as happened in *Mary* at the goal of this covenant.

35. Therefore, see to what you do. If you make a promise, then keep it: she would rather crown you than you could ever desire. But you must stand firm; when the tempter approaches you with the world’s lust, beauty, and glory, your mind <note>mind: original "Gemüthe," referring to the deep-seated disposition or center of the soul’s will.</note> must reject it and say: "I shall be a servant in the vineyard of *Christ*, and not a master; of all that I have, I am but a servant of **God** over it, and shall do with it as His Word teaches me; my heart shall always be simple in the dust and remain humble."

36. Whatever your station in life may be, humility must be at the forefront; otherwise, you will not attain her marriage, although true humility is only truly born within that marriage. However, your soul's free will must stand like a knight: for if the Devil cannot prevail with the soul's vanity—because she will not take his bait—he then comes with "unworthiness" and a "register of sins"; at that point, it becomes a matter of struggle.

37. Here, *Christ’s* merit must be placed at the forefront; otherwise, the *creature* cannot triumph over the Devil. For things can go so terribly for some people here that even external reason thinks this person is senseless and possessed by the Devil. The Devil defends himself so cruelly in many, especially if he has held a great "robber-castle" <note>robber-castle: original "Raub-Schloß." A metaphor for a soul deeply entrenched in habitual sin or pride, which the Devil occupies like a fortified stronghold.</note> within them.

Here the Virgin—who reveals herself from the precious name of **JESUS**, along with **Christ** the Serpent-Treader <note>original: "Schlangen-Treter" — a reference to the prophecy in Genesis 3:15 that the offspring of the woman would crush the serpent's head</note> as the Anointed of **God**—steps toward the soul and kisses her with her sweetest love in her innermost essence, and impresses her love into the soul’s desire as a sign of victory; and here **Adam** rises from death in **Christ** according to his heavenly part. I cannot write of this, for there is no pen in this world equal to the task; for it is the Marriage of the Lamb, where the noble pearl is sown—with great triumph indeed, yet at first it is as small as a mustard seed, as **Christ** says.

39. When this marriage is over, the soul must now see to it that she keeps what she has promised to her Virgin, so that the little pearl-tree <note>original: "Perlen-Bäumlein"</note> may grow and increase. For the Devil will immediately come with his stormy weather, along with godless people who will despise it, mock it, and decry it as madness. There, a person must now step under the Cross in *Christ’s process* <term>process: original "Proceß." The spiritual journey where a believer's life mirrors the stages of Christ's life, especially his suffering and death to the world</term>; here it first becomes a matter of proving by deed that we let ourselves be called Christians! There he must let himself be proclaimed a fool and a godless man; indeed, his very best friends, who previously flattered him in the lust of the flesh, will now become his enemies, and though they do not know why, they hate him. Thus **Christ** covers his bride under the Cross so that she is not recognized in this world; the Devil also does this so that these children of **God** remain hidden, lest many such branches grow in his supposed garden. I set this down for the instruction of the reader of Christian mind, should such things befall him, to know what he must do.

### The First Little Book

...[do not leave] me in this distress; for I am indeed guilty of the sins which now rise up in my conscience; if you forsake me, I must sink. You have promised me in your Word: Though a mother should forget her child, which would be a painful thing indeed, yet you will not forget me; you have etched me into your hands—into your hands pierced through with sharp nails—and into your hollow side, from which blood and water ran, you have etched me. I, a poor human, caught in your wrath, can do nothing nor have any power before you now; I only sink myself into your wounds and death.

O great mercy of **God**, deliver me from the bonds of the Devil: I have no other refuge in anything but only in your holy wounds and death. Into you I sink in the anguish of my conscience; do with me as you will. In you I will now live or die, as you will; only let me die and pass away in your death; bury me only in your death, so that the anguish of hell may not touch me. Why should I plead my innocence before you, who tests my heart and kidneys <note>original: "Nieren" — in the biblical sense, the "reins" or kidneys were considered the seat of a person’s most secret emotions and conscience</note>, and sets my sins before my eyes? I am indeed guilty of them, and I surrender myself to your judgment; yet carry out your judgment over me through the death of my Redeemer **JESUS** Christ.

I plead to you, O righteous Judge, through the anguish of my Redeemer **JESUS** Christ, when He sweated bloody sweat in my place on the Mount of Olives; when He allowed Himself to be scourged for me before Pilate, and a crown of thorns to be pressed onto His head in mockery, so that His blood flowed from Him. O just **God**, you have indeed placed Him in my stead; He was innocent, and I am the guilty one for whom He suffered: why should I then despair in your wrath? Extinguish your anger in me now through His anguish, suffering, and death: I surrender myself entirely into His anguish, suffering, and death; in His anguish and suffering I will hold still before you <note>original: "stille halten" — a core concept in Böhme’s mysticism meaning to yield the will or remain quiet and receptive in the presence of God</note>; do with me as you will, only let me not depart from His anguish; for you have given me His anguish as a gift, and drowned your wrath in Him. And although I have not accepted such a thing, but have departed from Him and become faithless, you have nevertheless given me this precious pledge in my flesh and soul, since He has taken my flesh and soul into His Heavenly being,

I pray that the Holy CHRIST may become manifest and become Man within my faded image of the heavenly, spiritual corporality <note>term: "spiritual corporality" <gloss>the "heavenly flesh" or spiritual body that Boehme believed humanity lost at the Fall and must regain through rebirth</gloss></note>, and that the poor soul may receive its dear bride back into its arms, with whom it may eternally rejoice.

> O IMMANUEL <note>Hebrew: "God with us."</note>, you marriage-state of God and man, into the arms of your desire toward and within us I surrender myself; for you I long: Do blot out your Father’s wrath with your love in me, and strengthen my weak image in me, that it may overcome and tame the vanity in flesh and blood, and serve you in holiness and righteousness.

> O great, most holy name and power of God, JEHOVAH, you who—in the promised goal of the covenant made with Adam our father—have moved with your most sweet power of JESUS in the "seed of the woman" <note>A reference to Genesis 3:15, interpreted by Christians as the first prophecy of Christ's birth from the Virgin Mary.</note>, the Virgin Mary, in our faded heavenly humanity. You have introduced your living essence of your holy power—within the Virgin Wisdom of God <note>term: "Virgin Wisdom" <gloss>also known as Sophia, she represents the mirror of God and the spiritual blueprint of humanity in Boehme’s mystical system</gloss></note>—into our humanity that had faded away from you, and have given us to life, victory, and new rebirth. I pray to you with all my strength: do give birth to me also in your sweet power of JESUS into a new and holy life, so that I may be in you, and you in me, and your kingdom may become manifest in me, and my soul’s will and conduct may be in heaven.

45. ### Summaries.

Man should take a serious intent, §. 1. examine himself, 2. and behold his will. 3-6. If he feels the desire for conversion, it is God's voice. 7. Accordingly, he should examine his life in God's commandments, 8. so that he may see which image is in him; 9. thus he will find a beast and a devil within himself. 10. There he must immediately strive to go out from the animal-like will <term>animal-like will: "thierischen Willen," the lower, instinctive nature driven by earthly desires rather than spirit</term>, 11. and take Christ’s promise into his heart and pray. 12. He should despair of his own ability, but not of God's grace, 13. but remain hanging fast to Christ’s promise, 14. fix his will, and pray constantly; 15. thus he will feel powers, 16. and come worthily to the marriage of the Lamb. 17. 18.

Whichever person wishes to attain to Divine contemplation <term>contemplation: "Beschaulichkeit," the state of inner vision or mystical observation of God</term> within themselves and talk with God in Christ, let them follow this process <term>process: "Proceß," the systematic spiritual method or path of transformation</term>, and they shall arrive at it.

### The Second Little Book.
->C 5<-

...that he may be a child of grace <term>child of grace: "Gnaden-Kind," a person living under divine favor and mercy rather than the strict judgment of the law</term> solely in Christ’s love, and see how far he has strayed from it, and what his daily practice and desire are: then this same drawing of the Father will lead him into God’s righteousness, and show him the ingrained images <note>original: "eingemodelten Bilder," referring to the internal archetypes or idols the soul has shaped for itself</note> in his heart which he has loved instead of God, and which he has held—and still holds—as his greatest treasure.

9. These images will be: (1) **Pride**, loving oneself and wanting to be honored by others. Likewise, it will be an image of power and authority in his pride, wanting to rise in honor above others. (2) Likewise, it will be the image of a **sow**, namely **Greed**, which wants to have everything for itself alone: and even if he possessed the world and heaven, he would still want to rule over hell; he who desires more than he needs for temporal life and has no faith in God within him, but is a filthy sow that desires to draw everything into itself. (3) Likewise, there will be in him an image of **Envy**, which stings other hearts and begrudges others if they have more temporal goods and honors than he. (4) Likewise, it will be **Anger**, where envy rises up within as a spirit, and for the slightest cause seeks to push, strike, rage, and justify itself. (5) Likewise, there will be a heap, even many hundreds of earthly beasts within him which he loves: for everything that is in the world, he loves, and has placed it in Christ's stead, and honors it more than God. Let him only look at his words, how his mouth secretly slanders other people and causes trouble among his own, often repeating gossip without certain grounds, rejoicing in his neighbor's misfortune and wishing it upon him: all of which are the claws and talons <note>original: "Klauen und Kreilen"</note> of the devil and the image of the serpent, which he carries within himself.

10. Then let him look at these in the light of God's Word in the Law and the Gospel, and he will see that he is more a beast and a devil than a true human being; and he will clearly see how these imagined and inherited images hold him back from God’s kingdom and lead him astray. So often, even when he would gladly do penance and turn toward God, these devil-claws hold him back and lead him away, and they suggest these masks <term>masks: "Larven," meaning false appearances or illusory personas that disguise the soul's true, corrupted state</term> of holiness to the poor soul, so that it enters back into its own lusts and remains sitting in God’s wrath, and finally steps into the abyss <term>abyss: "Abgrund," the "bottomless" state of existence separated from God's light</term> when the grace and the drawing of the Father are extinguished within it.

11. ### The Second Booklet

Let him impress this promise upon himself and make such a stern resolution <term>Fürsatz: A "resolution" or "firm purpose" in this spiritual context is a focused act of the will to turn toward God.</term> within himself that he will not depart from the promised grace of God in Christ, even if his body and soul should burst. 15. If he is a child of death, then he wishes to be in Christ’s promise within Christ’s death, and to die and live for Him as He wills. He must only direct his resolution into constant prayer and sighing to God, and surrender all his beginnings and deeds into the work of His hands, and be still from the imagination <term>Einbildung: More than just "fantasy," this refers to the active power of the mind to "form" or "image" its internal reality.</term> of greed, envy, and pride. Let him only surrender these three beasts, and the others will very soon also begin to become weak and sick, and approach death. Then Christ, through His promised words which the person envisions and wraps himself in, will take on a form for life and will begin to work within him; therein his prayer will become more powerful, and he will (the longer it continues) be more and more strengthened in the spirit of grace.

16. Just as a seed works and grows into a child in the mother's womb, despite many buffetings of nature and external accidents, until the child receives its life in the mother's womb: so it also happens here. The more a person departs from himself and out of the "images," the more he enters into God; until at last Christ becomes living in the embodied grace...

...becomes alive, which occurs through the great earnestness of the resolution. We admonish him in a Christian spirit to follow us in this process; thus he will come to **Divine Contemplation** within himself and hear what the **Lord** says through Christ within him. And herewith we commend him to the love of Christ.

# The Second Booklet,
## BOOK OF PRAYERS, <note>original: "LIBER PRECATIONUM"</note>
### or
# On Holy Prayer,
->arranged<-
### for every day of the week:

How man should constantly remember his office, station, and conduct, in which **God** has ordained him; and how he should commit his beginning, middle, and end in all his doing to **God**, and always work all his works with **God**; just as the branch of the tree bears its twigs with the power of the root, and carries its fruit upon them; and how he should, in all beginnings, draw strength for his working from **God’s** little fountain, and thank his Creator for every benefit.

->Alongside heartfelt contemplation of the suffering,<-
->death, and resurrection of **Jesus Christ**,<-

How man should always lead the hunger and desire of his soul through **Christ's** death into His resurrection in **God**, and press toward the new rebirth, so that he may pray in spirit and in truth, and the **Spirit of Christ** may pray in and with him, and intercede for him before **God**.

Composed at the request and desire of his dear and good friends, for their daily exercise of true Christianity in their little <term>Heart- and house-churches: A central concept in Böhme’s mysticism, suggesting that true worship happens within the individual heart and the private home, rather than being confined to a church building.</term>

->In the year 1624,<-
->by<-
## Jacob Boehme.

## The Author's Preface to the God-loving Reader.
### On the true foundation of the right art of prayer: what prayer is, and why God bids us to pray.

->Summaries.<-

Praying is not merely a common speaking of words. §. 1. as the mouth only creates a form of the will without power, about which God complains through the prophet. 2. 3. If we wish to pray rightly, we should consider well whether our heart seeks something for itself, 4. or only God’s mercy? 5. solely God's honor and the neighbor’s benefit, 6. in universal love? 7. not out of one's own strengths, 8. but in the name of JESUS. 9. In this, we should flee sin and surrender ourselves entirely to God. 10. What true praying is in faith, humility, and hope. 11. 12. Whoever prays thus will immediately hear God within themselves, 13. and feel God’s love. 14. But the Holy Spirit itself must pray within us, 15. for we have received a childlike <note>or "filial"</note> spirit. 16. Why Christ taught us to pray. 17. What hinders the hearing of prayer. 18. If one wishes to pray rightly, one should step before God "creatureless" <term>creaturlos: a mystical term meaning detached from worldly desires and created things</term> and purely with the will and mind, and pay no heed to the Devil’s grip; 19. but forgive one's enemies. 20. The soul must be bare and of pure will, and wrestle with God, 21. pay no heed to intruding thoughts, 22. nor doubt; 23. thus it works with God and brings forth good fruit. 24. etc.

Dear Christian reader! Praying rightly is not merely a habit, such that one only needs to speak the words of the prayer: No, such word-speaking, without heartfelt devotion and Divine desire, is only an external thing, an external formation of words.

2. The mouth forms its words of prayer only with the external power of the stars and the elements <note>This refers to the contemporary belief that the physical body and "animal soul" were influenced by the movements of the planets and the four elements</note>; and makes only a form of the will, in which there is no true, effective power

...power: for nothing pleases God except what He Himself works and does through a thing.

3. For God complains through the Prophet regarding such external mouth-prayer <note>original: "Mund-Gebet"</note> lacking power, where He says: *With their lips they draw near to me, but their heart is far from me* (Isaiah 29:13). Likewise Christ says: *Not everyone who says to me, "Lord, Lord," shall enter the kingdom of heaven, but he who does the will of my Father in heaven.* (Matthew 7:21.) And He spoke further in another place: *Without me you can do nothing.* (John 15:5.) He alone is the living source and the **Throne of Grace**, with and through which we can press forward with prayer before and into God.

4. If we wish to pray rightly, we should (1.) look at ourselves and well-consider whether our heart has formed itself into any other creature? <note>Meaning: whether the heart is more attached to worldly, created things than to the Creator.</note> And whether such a desire, as that which we seek to obtain from God, be right? Whether our desire, which we bring to God in prayer, is against the benefit and the love of our neighbor? Whether we seek temporal things therein to the detriment of our neighbor, drawing what is theirs to ourselves? Do we desire a universal love and harmony through it? Or do we seek only our own profit with such praying?

5. Secondly, (2.) we should well-consider whether we desire and love anything in our prayer more than the mercy of God? Whether we desire that which we seek of temporal things solely and alone from the Divine hand and cooperation? <term>Mitwirkung: the theological concept of "synergy" or God working alongside and through human actions.</term> Or do we wish to obtain it through our own skill, cunning, and wit, and only ask God for permission afterward? Do we rely upon ourselves? Or do we wish to obtain it through Divine cooperation, so that we may afterwards say with a joyful heart: "God has bestowed this upon me through His fatherly providence; I have only been the hand and the instrument"? Or do we wish to say: "I have brought this about through my own skill and understanding"?

6. Thirdly, (3.) we should consider what we intend to do with that which we ask and desire of God? Do we desire through it only the world’s honor and high standing for temporal pleasure? Or do we wish to use that which God grants us through our prayer with His blessing also for His honor,

11. Dear Christian reader! You should well consider what prayer is, and why God commands us to pray. It is not a thing like stepping before a worldly king or lord when one has offended him, asking him for grace while often thinking something quite different in one's heart. No; rather, it is a departure from oneself <note>original: "Ausgang seiner selber"</note>, so that a person surrenders themselves to God with all their powers, with all that they are, and all that they possess. Indeed, through true prayer, one surrenders oneself to be God's own property. He returns with the **Prodigal Son** to the Father in his first fatherland and inheritance, from which Adam, our first father, led us out. He no longer has any natural right to heavenly goods; he lost them all with Adam's departure, and consumed them through the **Devil’s harlotry** <term>Buhlerey: used here to describe the soul's illicit or unfaithful devotion to worldly vanity instead of God</term> in vanity.

12. So now, in great **humility** and **faith**, in true hope of God’s offered grace in His Son **Jesus Christ**, he must come to God with the Prodigal Son. In such a working, He also blots out sin within us, drowns it in the death of **Christ**, destroys hell, and brings forth the gates of eternal life (as the payment of **Christ**) within us through the wrath of **God** <note>This likely refers to the "wrath" being transformed into love through Christ’s sacrifice.</note>. He takes the devil’s power away from us and bears witness to **Christ** within us, so that in the spirit and merit of **Christ**, we cry out and speak to the Father of all mercy: **Abba** <note>original: "Abba," an Aramaic term for Father, denoting deep intimacy.</note>, dear Father!

Let none of this lead you astray; the power is in the inner ground <term>Inner ground (inwendiger Grund): A mystical term referring to the deepest, most essential part of the soul where the human meets the Divine.</term>, in the longing of the will, and it works with **God**. Only stand still, and wait for the **Lord**; it will surely break through at last, so that you will feel it in your heart and thank **God**.

And I commend you all into the active love of Jesus Christ, and myself into your brotherly and Christian favor.

27. Christian, dear reader! Praying rightly is also **true earnestness**, and must be earnest, or it is invalid before God. For if we wish to pray rightly, we should think of nothing else than that we stand before God’s clear countenance, before the Holy Trinity and the choirs of His holy angels; and that God, in our prayer, examines our soul, spirit, and heart, and looks upon our will most intimately to see if it is directed entirely toward Him, and if the will has surrendered itself completely to Him.

28. And if that is so, He touches the will with the power of His Holy Spirit and **shatters** it <note>original: "zerschellet," a mystical term for breaking the ego or self-will so that it may be rebuilt by God.</note>, so that it may become truly desirous and hungry for grace, and so that it begins to press out of itself in earnest and penetrate into God's mercy.

29. For in its own strength, the will is far too weak; but when the Divine power touches it, it is awakened so that it becomes fiery and truly desirous: in which desire God Himself works. Only then does the person speak rightly with God, and God truly speaks with the soul of the person.

## II. On Holy Prayer.

30. Such speaking or working is nothing else than that the poor soul eats of **God’s** mercy (which He has turned back toward us through the death of **Christ**) and refreshes itself with the balsam of **Divine** love in **Christ**, wherein it becomes strong against the temptation of the devil.

31. For the **Divine** hearing is the power of grace, which He has introduced into humanity again in the name of **Jesus**, and has opened there for us once more an open gate to His hearing, through which we can hear **God** truly speaking in us, as He speaks His mercy into us through that same opened gate of grace; and in return, the soul speaks through that same open gate within itself with **God**, and in such conversation is fed and refreshed, as well as enlightened and renewed, by **God’s** speaking.

32. For the soul eats of the out-breathing of **God** that became human, as the flesh and blood of **Christ**, in the same way and manner as a plant eats the power of the sun into itself, by which it becomes <term>tinged</term> <note>original: "tingiret," from the Latin *tingere*, meaning to dye or imbue. In this context, it refers to a spiritual transformation or "tincture" where the soul is permeated by the Divine essence.</note>, balsamic, and good, so that it grows and blooms; so also does the soul from the **Divine** Sun, from which it becomes light and powerful.

33. This is now the use and fruit of true prayer: a benefit which no external mouth or will turned away from **God** may reach; but rather only the inward-turned will, which gives itself entirely to **God**.

34. If such a thing is to happen, then the will must turn away from all other creatures and from all earthly things, and stand purely before **God**, so that the business of the creatures, or that which he wishes to ask of **God** in temporal things, only follows in the flesh and stands behind the pure will; this is so that the pure will may bring the body's necessity before **God**, and the flesh itself with its desires does not interfere; otherwise, it introduces earthly desire into the **Divine** activity of the soul.

35. Therefore, a true repentance and inward humility always belong to right, earnest prayer if we wish to obtain anything from **God**. For right praying is a "taking" of that which the soul desires, of which **Christ** says:
> From now on the kingdom of heaven suffers violence, and those who do violence seize it for themselves. (Matthew 11:12) <note>The author uses this verse to emphasize that prayer is an active, forceful spiritual grasping of God's grace, rather than a passive request.</note>

<header>II. On Holy Prayer.</header>

I establish this preparation—how a person should prepare themselves beforehand—when they wish to bring their short prayers and petitions before **God**. For one may be heard just as well in a short prayer as with many words, provided that the heart stands rightly before **God**. It requires no long-winded words, but only a faithful, repentant soul that gives itself over with total earnestness into the mercy of **God**, into **God’s** compassion. For a single sigh works with **God** if the will stands purely before **God** and has cast off the earthly garment, such as false desire: offered as a reminder to the reader and for their own encouragement.

37. For it is not strictly necessary to use only such a form of confession, rather the **Holy Spirit** will likely create a form within the heart itself when the will turns truly and earnestly to **God**.

38. Merely as a guide for those who do not yet know how a true petitioner should be prepared, I wish to set down this confession to guide their soul; and I will entrust the work of confession together with the prayer to the **Holy Spirit** in every soul that is truly earnest. He will likely create the confession and prayer within them. If one only approaches the gate with true earnestness—where **God** the **Lord** truly speaks within the human being—one will perceive it.

### A Thanksgiving of the Penitent Soul for the Bitter Suffering and Death of Jesus Christ.

51. **O** most profound love of **God** in **Christ Jesus!** I give you praise and thanks that you have redeemed me from the fire-torment of anguish <note>original: "Feuer-Quall der Peinlichkeit"—In 17th-century German, "Peinlichkeit" refers to agonizing pain or torment, and "Quall" (modern: Qual) relates to a boiling or surging source of suffering.</note>, and have entered yourself with your love and grace into my fire-torment, and transformed me into a love-fire and Divine light. Amen.

Refers to the Lord's Supper or Eucharist as a spiritual feast.</note> of your eternal covenant in **Christo JEsu**, and I pray you, sanctify my poor soul in the Sabbath of your Son **JEsu Christi**, and lead her therein into the eternal rest, and give her again the food of your true Sabbath, which is his holy flesh and blood, so that my soul may again sanctify your Sabbath, and you alone may work in her, as in your image <note>original: "Ebenbilde." Refers to the *Imago Dei*, the concept of man being created in the likeness of God.</note>.

Break, then, the devil’s Sabbath and false working within me, and give me an obedient heart that constantly hungers after your Sabbath, and let your Word keep the Sabbath in me, so that my soul may hear what you speak in your working within me, so that she may be obedient to you, and I may place all my trust in you alone.

O you eternal Love, **JEsu Christe**, how glorious is your Sabbath in the soul when she turns to you, so that you permeate her with your sweet love, in which Paradise is opened to her once more! Let my soul dwell eternally in your Sabbath; build up in me again the New Jerusalem, as the City of God, in which your Sabbath is sanctified. I surrender myself completely to your Sabbath; deliver me only from evil. Amen.

O Eternal **God**, through our physical parents you present to us an image of our Eternal Father and our Eternal Mother: for you are our Father, from whom we have received our life, and your Word is our Mother, who has born us out of your creation and formed us according to the image <note>original: "Ebenbilde." A reference to the *Imago Dei*, the theological concept of being created in the likeness of God.</note> of your revelation. Our soul and mind, O **God** Father, are your image, and our body is an image of your expressed Word, which Word is our eternal Mother, in whose womb we are conceived and nourished: we should honor her, and humble ourselves before her, and be obedient to her. Just as we should honor our external, physical parents, so also should we honor our Eternal parents, from whose foundation we have sprouted.

O Eternal Father, we have become disobedient to you and have given ourselves over to the care of a foreign mother: we have accepted the World as our mother, and have become unfaithful to the inward Mother of your power in your Word. Now we must suck poison and death into ourselves from the breasts of this foreign mother; indeed, she now carries us in her womb of adversity, bears us and consumes us again in your wrath <note>original: "Grimm." In this mystical context, it refers to the harsh, judging quality of nature apart from divine love.</note>, and nourishes us for the duration of this entire outward life in pure misery, sorrow, toil, and distress, in suffering and want, and keeps us imprisoned within herself so that we cannot see our true eternal Mother; our soul laments for her, but your anger keeps us imprisoned, so that we must serve the foreign mother.

O **God**, how long will you forget us in our misery! Take us back again as your children, and bear us anew in our eternal Mother, and give us an obedient will, so that we may never deviate from you again throughout eternity.

Give us also an obedient heart toward our physical parents, that we may love and honor them as your divine ordinance <note>original: "Ordnung." Referring to the natural and spiritual order established by God.</note>, since you bear us through them into this world and to the light—

3. ### Ch. 1. III. Of True Resignation.

4. ...nature, to become great and mighty, and moreover to become more clever: just as **Lucifer** in his **Center** <term>Centrum: the core or inner source of a being's life</term> sought the **Fire-Mother** <note>In Böhme’s thought, the "Fire-Mother" refers to the harsh, energetic source of life that must be tempered by God's light</note>, and intended thereby to rule over **God’s** love and the entire angelic host; and **Adam** also desired to taste the "Mother" from which Evil and Good flow, in the essence, and directed his desire into it, with the will to become clever and intellectually wise through it.

5. Consequently, **Lucifer** remained stuck in the fierce, dark torment of fire, and that same fire became manifest in his will-spirit, whereby the creature, in its desire, became an enemy of the love and gentleness of **God**.

6. So too was **Adam** immediately seized by the earthly Mother (which is both Evil and Good, being created as a single being out of **God's** love and wrath). The earthly property immediately gained governance in **Adam**, from which it happened that heat and cold, envy, anger, and all false ill-will and malice against **God** became manifest and dominant in him.

8. In this same way, such a thing still brings danger today to the enlightened children of **God**: when the sun of the great vision of **God’s** holiness shines upon someone, from which their life enters into a state of triumph, **reason** reflects itself therein, and the **will** enters into **selfhood** (as if into its own private research). It wants to test the **Center** from which the light shines and force itself into it through its own power.

9. It thinks it may do whatever it wants, and that it is **God's** will acting in it, or that it is a prophetess; and yet it is only within itself, following its own desire, in which the **Center** of the creature very soon [soars]

# III. Of True Resignation. Chap. 1.

18. And so it goes for all those who are once enlightened by **God**, and then depart from true **Resignation** <term>Gelassenheit: the spiritual practice of surrendering one's own will and ego to God</term>, and wean themselves from the true mother’s breasts—that is, from right **Humility**.

### The Process of a True Christian, and How He Should Walk.

19. **Reason** will object to me and say: it is surely right and good that a person attains the light of **God**, as well as the light of outer nature and **Reason**, so that he may govern his life wisely, according to **Holy Scripture**.

20. Yes, it is right, and nothing more useful or better can happen to a person—it is a treasure above all treasures of this world—whoever may reach and obtain the light of **God** and of **Time** <note>The "light of Time" refers to natural knowledge and understanding of the physical world</note>; for it is an eye of **Time** and **Eternity**.

21. But hear how you should use it: the light of **God** first opens itself in the **Soul**; it shines out like a light from a candle, and immediately kindles the outer **Light of Reason**—not so that it should give itself over entirely to the **Reason** (as the outer man) for its own governance; no, the outer man beholds himself in that penetrating shine, like an image before a mirror, and he immediately learns to know himself in **Selfhood** <term>Selbheit: the state of being centered on the ego or "I"</term>, which in itself is good and useful.

22. Now when this happens, **Reason** (as the creaturely **Selfhood**) can do nothing better than to ensure it does not gaze upon itself in the **Selfhood** of the creature, and that it does not enter into the **Center** <term>Centrum: the inner core of the soul where spiritual forces are birthed</term> with the will of desire and seek itself; otherwise, it breaks itself off from **God’s Being** (which rises up within the light of **God**, and upon which the soul should eat and refresh itself) and eats from the outer light and being, whereby it draws the poison back into itself.

# Ch. 1. III. Of True Resignation.

23. The will of the **Creature** <note>original: "Creatur"; Böhme uses this to refer to the human being as a created entity, distinct from the Creator</note> should, with all its reason and desire, sink itself completely down, like an unworthy child who is not at all deserving of such high grace. 24. # III. Of True Resignation. Ch. 1.

[The soul must have a] desire to sink itself into that same light, and to consider itself unworthy and as nothing.

27. Thus, the soul's own desire penetrates into **Nothingness** <note>original: "Nichts"; for Böhme, this "Nothingness" is not a void, but a state free from selfish desires where God's will can operate</note>, desiring only **God’s** works and actions—doing what He wills within it. In this way, the human **Selfhood** <note>original: "Selbheit"</note> follows after the Spirit of **God** in the trembling and joys of humility; and thus it may behold everything that is in time and eternity, for everything is near to it.

28. When the Spirit of **God** moves as a fire of the flame of love, then the will-spirit of the soul sinks down and says: "Lord, to Your name be the glory, and not to me. You have the power to take strength, power, might, wisdom, and knowledge; do what You will. I can do nothing and know nothing; I will go nowhere unless You lead me as Your **instrument** <note>original: "Werkzeug"; a key Böhme concept where the human becomes a passive tool for divine action</note>. Do in and with me whatever You will."

29. In such humble and total **surrender** <note>original: "Einergeben"</note>, the spark of Divine power falls like tinder into the **center of the life-form** <note>original: "Centrum der Lebens-Gestaltniß"</note>—that is, into the **soul-fire** which **Adam** had turned into a dark coal—and it begins to glow. And as the light of Divine power then ignites within it, the **Creature** <note>the human being</note> must then step forward as an instrument of the Spirit of **God** and speak what the Spirit of **God** says. It is then no longer its own property, but the instrument of **God**.

30. But the soul's will must also, without ceasing, sink itself into this fiery drive toward **Nothingness**, into the highest humility before **God**. As soon as it wishes to proceed with even the smallest part of its **own searching** <note>original: "eigenem Forschen"; intellectual effort independent of divine grace</note>, the Devil reaches it in the center of its life-form and **sifts it** <note>an allusion to Luke 22:31, where Satan desires to "sift" the disciples like wheat</note> so that it enters back into **Selfhood**. Therefore, it must remain in resigned humility, just like a spring at its source, and must without ceasing draw and drink from **God’s** little fountain, never desiring to depart from **God’s** ways.

31. For as soon as the soul eats from its **Selfhood**, from the **light of reason** <note>original: "Vernunft-Licht"; human logic as opposed to divine revelation</note>, it wanders in its own delusion. Then the things it presents as Divine are merely the influence of the **outer constellation** <note>original: "ausseren Constellation"; the astrological or worldly influences of the physical universe (the macrocosm) which Böhme believed could mislead the mind</note>, which immediately seizes the soul and makes it drunk. Thus it runs in error for as long as it takes to surrender itself entirely back into **resignation**, presenting itself once more as a soiled child...

32. 33. They should desire to learn or want nothing unless they find themselves in true resignation, so that **God’s** Spirit may teach, lead, and guide the spirit of man, and so that the human self-will—aimed at its own pleasure—may be entirely broken and yielded to **God**.

34. 35. I do not say that man should research or learn nothing in the natural arts: no, for that is useful to him; but one's own reason should not be the beginning. Man should not govern his life solely through the <term>outer light of reason</term> <note>original: "äusser Vernunft-Licht"; the intellect unaided by divine revelation or spiritual insight</note>. That light is indeed good, but he should sink himself with it into the deepest humility before **God**, and place the Spirit and Will of **God** at the forefront of all his research, so that the light of reason sees through **God’s** light. And even if reason gains much knowledge, it should not take credit for it as a personal possession, but give the glory to **God**, to whom alone belong knowledge and wisdom.

What the good builds, the evil breaks; and what the evil builds, the good breaks. ### III. On True Resignation. Ch. 2.
<meta>catchword: he</meta>

[de]sire stands in the Center <note>original: "Centro"; Böhme uses this term to describe the inner core or source-point of a being's nature</note> of the eternal, beginningless nature; whichever it ignites itself within—whether in Evil or Good—it carries out the effect of that same thing.

15. Now, God has created every thing into that wherein it ought to be, such as the angels in Heaven, and man in Paradise. But if the desire of the creature <note>original: "Creatur"</note> departs from its own mother <note>The "mother" refers to the divine source or the essential "womb" of nature from which the creature originated.</note>, it enters into opposition and enmity; and therein it is tormented with that opposition, and a false will arises within a good one. Because of this, the good will returns into its "Nothingness"—as if to the very boundary of nature and creature—and abandons the creature in its own malice. This can be seen in the case of Lucifer, and also in Adam: had God's Will of Love not met him again and entered into humanity once more through grace, there would likely still be no good will within man.

16. Therefore, all speculating and searching into God's will, without a turning of the mind <note>original: "Umwendung des Gemüthes"; this implies a fundamental conversion or internal redirection of one's disposition</note>, is a vain thing. When the mind stands imprisoned in its own desire for this earthly life, it cannot grasp God's will; it only runs in selfhood <note>original: "Selbheit"; the state of being centered on the ego rather than God</note> from one path to another, and yet finds no rest: for one's own desire always introduces unrest.

17. But when it sinks itself entirely into God’s mercy, and desires to die to its selfhood, and desires God's will as its guide and understanding—so that it recognizes and holds itself as a Nothing that wills nothing except what God wills—then, when the desire of Wrath <note>original: "Zorns Begierde"</note> comes from the earthly flesh through the devil’s imagination <note>original: "Imagination"; in Böhme’s terminology, this refers to the soul's power to "image" or pull itself into a particular state or reality</note> and strikes against the soul's will, the resigned desire cries out to God:
> Abba, dear Father, deliver me from evil! <note>original: "Abba lieber Vater, erlöse mich vom Uebel!"</note>

and it then works (even if it should happen that the earthly will becomes too strong in the wrath of God through the devil's craving) only within itself, just as St. Paul also says:
> If I now sin, it is not I who do it, but the sin that dwells in the flesh. Romans 7:20. <note>original: "Röm. 7, 20"</note>

33. There is no other way to God than a new mind that turns away from malice and enters into repentance for its committed sins, departs from evil-doing and desires it no longer; but rather winds its will into Christ’s death, and earnestly dies to the sins of the soul in Christ’s death, so that the soul’s mind no longer desires sin. 34. An entirely new will must arise out of Christ’s death; indeed, it must be born out of Christ’s entry into humanity and arise in Christ’s resurrection.

35. The poor imprisoned soul must earnestly wind itself into the dying of Christ with all that it is, so that the son of the bondwoman (the sin within her) may die in Christ’s death. Yes, sin must die in the soul's will, otherwise there can be no beholding of God; for the earthly will in its sins and God's wrath shall not behold God, but rather Christ, who came into the flesh. The soul must put on Christ’s spirit and flesh: in this earthly hut <note>A metaphor for the physical body.</note> she cannot inherit God’s kingdom, even though the kingdom of sin clings to her from the outside, which must rot in the earth and arise in new power.

### Ch. 2. III. On True Resignation.
<header>Cap. 2. III. Von wahrer Gelassenheit.</header>

...to name <note>original: "nennen" — the sentence concludes from the previous page: "indeed, it must be born out of God to name them children born of God..."</note> them children born of God, with a new man who has surrendered himself into God.

37. All hypocrisy—wherein we say that Christ has paid the debt and done enough to satisfy for sin, that He died for our sin—is entirely false and a delusion (a futile, invalid comfort) if we do not also die to sin in Him, put on His merit in a new obedience, and live within it.

38. Only he who becomes an enemy to sin and feels a bitterness toward it has the right to comfort himself with Christ’s suffering; he who does not like to see, hear, or taste it; he who is its enemy; he who would always gladly do right and well if he only knew what he should do: that person has put on <note>original: "angezogen" — to "clothe" oneself in something, a biblical metaphor for spiritual transformation.</note> Christ’s Spirit and will. The outward hypocrisy of an externally assumed "childship" is false and worthless.

39. It is not the work performed in the outer flesh alone that creates "childship" <note>original: "Kindschaft" — the state of being a child of God.</note>; rather, it is the working of Christ in the spirit, which is powerful alongside the outer work and reveals itself as a new light, manifesting this childship in the outer works of the flesh—that is what constitutes and creates childship.

40. For if the eye of the soul is light, then the whole body is light in all its members. Now, if someone boasts of being a child of God yet allows the body to burn in sins, he is not yet capable of childship, or is indeed caught in the bonds of the devil, imprisoned in a heavy darkness. And if he does not find the earnest will for doing good burning within him in love, then his claim is merely a <term>fabrication of reason</term> <note>original: "Vernunft-Tichten" — intellectual constructs or "figments" created by the human mind rather than spiritual revelation.</note> arising from <term>selfhood</term> <note>original: "Selbheit" — the ego-driven state of being centered on oneself rather than yielding to the divine.</note>, which cannot behold God unless it be born anew and manifest itself in the power of childship. For no fire exists without radiance. If God’s fire is in the mind, it will surely shine forth and do what God wants done.

41. To this you might say: "I have the will for it; I would gladly do it, but I am held back; I cannot."

42. Yes, dear stained little piece of wood <note>original: "besudeltes Hölzel" — a humble, slightly stinging metaphor for the human soul as a piece of fuel that is too damp or dirty to catch the divine fire.</note>, that is exactly it; God draws you toward childship, but you do not want it; your soft kissing of evil is much dearer to you; you prefer the joy of earthly malice over God’s joy; you are still entirely stuck in selfhood and live according to the law of sin—that is what holds you. You do not wish to die to the <term>lusts of the flesh</term>; therefore, you are not in a state of childship, and God...

<summary>This page argues that salvation requires a genuine internal transformation (dying to sin) rather than just an intellectual acceptance of Christ's sacrifice. Böhme emphasizes that true "childship" with God must manifest as visible "light" or good works, and identifies "selfhood" as the primary obstacle to this rebirth.</summary>

...[it] draws you toward it; but you yourself do not want to go. 45. Therefore, it is not such an easy thing to become or to be children of God as people portray to us. It requires such a purpose that, even if body and soul should break apart because of it, the will would nonetheless remain constant and not return into selfhood.

46. There must be earnest prayer with great humility, and one must be a "fool" to one's own reason for a while—seeing oneself as foolish within it—until Christ takes on a form in this new incarnation.

47. And then, when Christ is born, Herod immediately arrives and wants to kill the infant; he seeks it from without through persecution, and from within through temptation, to see if this Lily-branch will be strong enough to break the Devil's kingdom, which is manifest in the flesh.

<page-num>107</page-num>
### Ch. 2. III. On True Resignation.

[The soul] leaves behind the earthly, and indeed even the outward life, for the sake of the childship. <note>original: "Kindschaft" — the spiritual status of being a child of God, involving a participation in the divine nature.</note>

49. No worldly honor or wealth must be preferred above the childship; rather, one must leave all that behind by his own will, and not regard it as his own, but consider himself only a servant of the same, who serves his Master in obedience with it. He must leave all the property of this world: not that he should not possess it or be allowed to possess it; but his heart must leave it, and not lead his will into it, nor regard it as his own; otherwise he has no power to serve the needy with it.

50. Selfhood <term>Selfhood: (German: *Selbheit*) Böhme’s term for the ego-driven, rebellious nature of the human will that seeks its own power and gratification apart from God.</term> serves only the temporal essence; but resignation <term>Resignation: (German: *Gelassenheit*) A central concept for Böhme, meaning a total surrender of the self-will to God, often translated as "yieldedness."</term> rules over everything that is beneath it. Selfhood must do what the devil wants in the lusts of the flesh and a prideful life; but resignation treads that under the feet of the mind. Selfhood despises what is simple; but resignation lays itself in the dust with the simple, saying: I will be simple and understand nothing, so that my understanding does not exalt itself and sin; I will lie at the feet in the courtyards of my **God**, so that I may serve my Master in whatever way He wants me; I will know nothing, so that the commands of my Lord may lead and guide me, and I may only do what **God** wants to do and have through me; I will sleep in my selfhood until the **Lord** awakens me with His Spirit; and if He does not so will, then I will rest eternally in Him in the stillness and await His command.

51. Dear brothers, people boast of faith nowadays; but where is that faith? Current faith is a mere history. <note>original: "Historia" — here meaning a purely intellectual or historical knowledge of the Bible (knowing the "story") without the living, transformative experience of Christ.</note> Where is the child who believes that **Jesus** is born? If it were so, and the child believed that **Jesus** was born, then it would surely approach the infant **Jesus**, and receive Him and care for Him. Alas, it is only a historical faith and a pure science <note>In this context, "science" refers to head-knowledge or academic learning without spiritual life.</note>, and more of a tickling of the conscience, that the Jews killed Him; that He departed from this world; that He is not King on earth in the animal man; <note>original: "animalischen Menschen" — the carnal, biological nature of humanity that remains unregenerated.</note> that man may do whatever he wants; that he does not need to die to sin and evil lusts. Selfhood, that wicked child, rejoices in this, so that it may live in fatness and fatten the devil.

## Preface of the *Author.*

Although I have sufficiently explained this in my other very deep writings and presented it from its foundation; however, since everyone does not have such books in hand, nor is it within everyone’s comprehension <term>Begriff: the intellectual capacity to grasp complex ideas</term> to understand them: I have, for the service of the simple children of Christ and at the request of good friends, written a short summary <note>original: *Summam*</note> of the new rebirth, so that someone might learn to know themselves through it.

# Chapter 1. IV. Of the New Rebirth.

4. Since it remains true that a true Christian is born of Christ, and that the new rebirth is a temple of the Holy Spirit who dwells within us, and that only the new man, born of Christ, partakes of the flesh and blood of Christ; then it is not such a trivial thing to be a Christian. Christianity does not consist in the history—<note>Böhme uses "history" to refer to a purely intellectual or literal acceptance of biblical events without an accompanying internal spiritual experience.</note> that we merely know it and claim that knowledge for ourselves, saying "Christ died for us, and has broken death within us and turned it into life; He has paid the debt for us, we need only take comfort in this and firmly believe it has happened."

5. For we find within ourselves that sin is alive, desiring, and active in the flesh; it is at work. Thus, the new rebirth from Christ must be something else—something that does not cooperate with the sinful flesh, and which does not want sin.

6. For St. Paul says that for those who are in Christ Jesus, there is nothing damnable. Romans 8:1. And further: Should we, who are Christians, still be found to be sinners? God forbid, Galatians 2:17. for we have died to sin (in Christ). Furthermore, the man of sin is not a temple of the Holy Spirit; and yet there is no man who does not sin; for the Scripture says: God has consigned all to sin. Romans 11:32. Likewise: before you no living being is righteous, if you choose to measure sin. Psalm 143:2. <note>The abbreviation Pl. or Pf. in the text refers to the Psalms.</note> The righteous fall seven times a day; Proverbs 24:16. yet this must not be understood to mean that the "righteous" [new man] falls and sins, but rather the mortal (and sinful) man.

7. For a Christian’s righteousness is in Christ, who cannot sin. For St. Paul says: Our conduct is in heaven, from whence we look for the Savior Jesus Christ. Philippians 3:20. If our conduct is now in heaven, then heaven must be within us. Christ dwells in heaven; if we are then His temple, then that same heaven must be within us.

8. But if sin nevertheless assails us—within which the devil has an entrance to us and into us—then hell must also be within us, for the devil dwells in hell. And wherever he is, he is in hell and cannot leave it; even if he were to possess a human being,

He distinguishes between the "new man" born of Christ, who is righteous, and the "mortal man" who continues to struggle with sin.</summary>

### IV. Of the New Rebirth. Chapter 1.

<meta>The text begins mid-sentence, continuing from the previous page's discussion of how God's presence or absence is felt within the human soul.</meta>

...vessel, yet he still dwells within man in hell, as in the wrath of God.

9. Now we must rightly consider man, what and how he may be; and that a true Christian is not merely a **historical** <note>Böhme uses "historical" to describe a faith that is only in the head—knowing the stories of the Bible without experiencing their power.</note> new man—that it is not enough for us to confess Christ and believe that He is the Son of God and has paid the debt for us. For it is not a matter of a righteousness **imputed from the outside**, where we only believe it has happened; rather, it is an **inborn, childlike** righteousness. Just as the flesh must die, so also must the life and the **will of sin** die; and one must become like a child that knows nothing and sighs only for the mother who gave it birth. Thus, the will of a Christian must enter entirely back into the mother—namely, into the **Spirit of Christ**—and in the "selfhood" of his own willing and ability, he must become a child whose will and desire are directed only toward the mother. Out of the Spirit of Christ, a new will and obedience in righteousness must arise from death, which no longer desires sin.

10. For the will that allows **vanity** <note>original: "Eitelkeit." In Böhme’s vocabulary, this refers to the empty, prideful, and fleeting nature of the material world that distracts from God.</note> into itself and desires it, is not born anew. And even though a will remains in the newborn person that longs for vanity and sins, we must rightly consider the image of man to see how the new rebirth occurs. Since it does not happen in the mortal flesh, yet it does truly happen within us—in flesh and blood, in water and spirit—as the Scripture says.

11. Thus we must rightly consider what kind of man is within us who is a **member** <note>original: "Gliedmaß." A limb or organic part of a larger body; here, part of the mystical body of Christ.</note> of Christ and a **temple of God** who dwells in heaven; and then also, what kind of man it is who dwells only in the outer world; and what kind of man it is whom the devil rules and drives. For he cannot rule or drive the temple of Christ, nor does he care for the mortal flesh; yet there are not three men within one another, but only one single man.

12. Now, if we wish to consider such things, we must consider **Time and Eternity**, how these are within one another; as well as Light and Darkness, Good and Evil; but especially man’s **original state** <term>original state</term> <note>original: "Urstand." This refers to the primal origin or foundational essence of a being's existence before its temporal manifestation.</note> and his source.

13. This is now to be considered as follows. We look at the outer...

We also have an example of this in the four elements, which in their original state <term>Urstand: a term used by Böhme to describe the primal, unmanifested source of all things</term> are only One Element, and that is neither hot nor cold, neither dry nor wet, and yet with movement it divides itself into four properties: fire, air, water, and earth.

14. Who would believe that fire could give birth to water? Or that the origin of fire could be in water, if we did not see this with our own eyes in sheet lightning? It is also found in living beings that the essential fire dwells in the **body** <note>original: "Corpore"</note> within the blood, and that the blood is its mother, and the fire is the father of the blood.

15. Just as **GOD** dwells in the world and fills everything, and yet possesses nothing; and as fire dwells in water and yet does not possess it; and as the light dwells in darkness and yet does not possess the darkness; day in night, and night in day; time in eternity, and eternity in time: so too is man created. According to his outward humanity, he is time and within time, and time is the outer world—that is also the outward man. And the inward man is eternity, and the spiritual time and world, which also stands in light and darkness: in **GOD’S** love according to the eternal light, and in **GOD’S** wrath according to the eternal darkness. Whichever of these is manifest within him, his spirit dwells there, either in the darkness or in the light. Both are in him, the light and the darkness; each dwells in itself, and neither possesses the other.

16. But if one enters into the other and wishes to possess the other, then the other loses its right and power. The suffering part <note>The "suffering" part refers to the element that is being acted upon or yields to the other.</note> loses its power; for when the light becomes manifest in the darkness, the darkness loses its darkness and is not recognized. Likewise, on the other hand, if the darkness rises up in the light and gains power, then the light with its power is extinguished.

# Chapter 3

->Summary<-

As Adam and Eve fell, the **Wrath of Nature** <term>Wrath of Nature (Grimm der Natur): The harsh, consuming, and non-harmonized state of nature that exists when it is separated from the light and love of God.</term> awoke in every property, and the soul became an animal in the body: §. 1. because of this, the heaven within man trembled, 2. and the earth was cursed for the sake of vanity. 3. Then the Seed of the woman was promised, who would crush the head of the serpent. 4. Thus God reconciled His wrath in the goal of the covenant: 5. and the goal of this covenant is propagated from person to person, 6. and became active in the seed of Mary, 7. where God's essence and man’s faded essence became One Person, 8. which is symbolized by the dry rod of Aaron. 9. Thus Christ became man, 10. He did not take on sinful flesh, 11. but He transformed hell within the human property into heaven. 12.

When Adam and Eve fell into this misery, the wrath of nature awoke in every property, and in its desire, it **impressed** <note>original: "impresseete." This refers to a spiritual contraction or hardening where spiritual essence becomes solid, "thick" physical matter.</note> the vanity of earthliness and the wrath of God into itself. Then the flesh became coarse and thick like that of any other animal, and the noble soul was thereby imprisoned in that essence. It looked upon itself and saw that it had become an animal in its body, and it saw the animal limbs for reproduction, and the **stinking sack of maggots** <note>original: "stinkenden Madensack." 2. At this, the heaven within man trembled before the cruelty: just as the earth trembled in wrath when this anger was broken on the Cross by the sweetest love of God; then the wrath trembled before the great love of God.
