## The Incarnation of JESUS Christ, Part 3.

119. There is no other way that is more correct than to depart from reason with the will, and not to seek oneself, but to cast oneself entirely into God’s love and God’s will, and to leave aside everything that reason throws in the way. Chapter 2, §. 7.

120. God’s will must become a master over reason if reason is to accomplish anything worthy that might stand before God: for nothing stands before God unless it be born in God’s will. Now, if the will turns toward God, the <term>will-spirit</term> <note>original: "Willen-Geist"; the driving force of human intent</note> becomes a child of God; and thus, the wonders performed with the spirit of reason also stand before God, for they are made in God’s will and are transferred from the temporal into the eternal. Chapter 3, §. 7.

121. This is the most painful thing, which enters most bitterly into a person when the <term>Tree of Faith</term> <note>original: "Glaubens-Baum"; a metaphor for the growth of spiritual conviction and life within the soul</note> is to be born in him: that he must lead his will-spirit out of his earthly treasure—such as pride, greed, envy, anger, and falsehood—and toward the Spirit of God. Chapter 5, §. 2.

122. The outer man should reveal the wonders of external nature, both in the <term>Outer Mystery</term> <note>original: "äussern Mysterio"; the physical universe seen as a manifestation of hidden divine secrets</note>, from the earth and above the earth: everything that the stars are capable of and that the earth contains, man should bring into wonder, form, and being, according to the eternal figure that was seen in God’s wisdom before the times of the world. But he should not set his will therein, nor regard those things as his treasure; he may use them only for his adornment and joy. However, with the inner man he should work in <term>God’s Mystery</term> <note>original: "Gottes Mysterio"; the spiritual or divine realm</note>, and then God’s Spirit will also help him to seek and find the outer things. Chapter 5, §. 7.

123. Because we have been so corrupted through the heavy <term>Fall of Adam</term> <note>the biblical narrative of humanity's original turn away from God</note>, it is highly necessary for us to depart from earthly splendor with our mind and will, and to seek ourselves first before we seek earthly finery; we must first learn to know where our true home is, and not make our minds earthly. Chapter 5, §. 8.

## Six Theosophical Points.

124. Life is the son of the essences, and the will, in which the figure of life stands, is the father of the essences: for no essence may arise without will, for in the will the desire is <term>originated</term> <note>original: "geurständet"; a term used by Jacob Böhme to describe the primary source, grounding, or "uprising" of a thing's existence</note>, in which the essences originate. Chapter 1, §. 6.

125. The <term>mind</term> <note>original: "Gemüth"; refers to the soul’s inner disposition, including the intellect and the will</note> is free and is the <term>pivot</term> <note>original: "Angel"; literally "hinge," referring to the point upon which the soul’s direction turns</note>, and it possesses understanding; it may weigh and turn toward wherever it wishes, and may stand by whichever principle it wishes. Chapter 2, §. 54.

126. Love does not let wrath into itself: now they are separated, and love thrusts the wrath away from itself, and the wrath also no longer desires the property of love. Chapter 4, §. 14.

127. Where the wills in the severe forms of nature wish to be masters, there is a separation and an eternal enmity; for one form always hates the other, and each one exalts itself. Chapter 5, §. 5.

## Six Mystical Points.

128. The inner imagination leads the outer will into the inner blood; by this, the blood and flesh of the Divine Essence are corrupted, and the noble image of God is darkened. Part 1, §. 7.

129. Love has only one <term>source-quality</term> <note>original: "Qual"; Böhme uses this word to imply both a "tormenting" fire and a "welling up" (quellen) of quality or life-force</note> and will; it desires only its own kind, and not many things; for the Good is only One, but the source-qualities are many. And whichever human will desires many things leads itself into the <insert>torment of</insert> multiplicity <note>The author contrasts the peace of the "One" (God) with the agitation and "darkness" of having many desires</note> (within which God dwells). For the "Something" is dark and darkens the light of life, and the One is light, for it loves itself, and there is no desire for more. Thus, the will of life must be directed into the One, as into the Good, so that it remains in a single source-quality. Part 3, §. 7. 8. 9.

130. Everything that is to subsist in God and wishes to be in Him must be free of its own will and walk in Him, in His will; it must have no fire of its own burning within itself, but God’s fire must be its fire; its will must be purified in God, so that God’s will and man’s will and spirit are only One. Part 3, §. 12. 21.

131. What is One does not hate itself; it has only one will;

132. Whatever desires to be in God must walk in Him, in His will. Since we in God are only one in many members, it is indeed against God if one member withdraws from another and makes a lord of itself. Part 3, § 21.

133. Here we must contemplate the Word of God that became man. If man sets his desire into it, he departs from the <term>agony</term> <note>original: "Qual"; a term used by Jacob Böhme to describe the painful tension or "source-quality" of existence within the forms of nature</note> of his own fire and is born anew in the Word. Thus, the outgoing will dwells in God, and the first [will] dwells in the desire of multiplicity. Part 3, § 24.

134. The will of life must be directed in struggle against itself: for it must flee from the wrath and not desire it; it must not desire the craving that its fire nonetheless wants and must also have. Part 3, § 27.

135. The <term>imagination</term> <note>In Böhme’s thought, this is the creative, image-forming power of the spirit</note> is gentle and soft, resembling water; but the desire is harsh and dry, like a hunger. Part 5, § 10.

136. <term>Magic</term> <note>original: "Magia"; referring to the formative, supernatural power of the will to manifest spirit into substance</note> creates divine flesh, and the understanding is from wisdom: it is a discerner of colors, powers, and virtues. The understanding leads the right, true spirit with a bridle; for the spirit is flying, and the understanding is its fire. Part 5, § 13.

137. The spirit does not deviate from the understanding, but rather it is the will of the understanding; however, the senses within the understanding are flying out and deviating. Part 5, § 14.

138. The senses are the lightning-flash from the fire-spirit; in the light, they carry within themselves the flames of majesty, and in the darkness, they carry the gaze of terror, like a wrathful lightning-flash from the fire. Part 5, § 15.

139. The understanding is the power-fire, and magic is the burning [fire], and yet it is only the mother to the fire. The fire is called the <term>principle</term> <note>original: "Principium"; the foundational source or beginning of a specific realm of existence</note>, and magic is called desire. Part 5, § 18.

140. The <term>mystery</term> <note>original: "Mysterium"; the hidden, unmanifested potential of the divine</note> is the magical will, which still sticks in the desire; it may form itself in the mirror of wisdom however it wishes. Part 6, § 1.

### Of True Repentance, First Book.

142. Our <term>mind</term> <note>original: "Gemüth"; the inner seat of a person's disposition, will, and soul</note> is turned away from God, seeking only earthliness, loving itself more than God and neighbor; it is held fast by three chains: God’s wrath, the devil’s desire, and earthly flesh and blood. § 1. 2. 3.

143. God can will nothing evil in the love of Christ, in the most precious name of JESUS; in this name there is no "glance of wrath"; He is the highest and deepest love and faithfulness, the greatest sweetness of the Godhead in the great name <term>JEHOVAH</term> <note>The Hebrew Tetragrammaton; Böhme often analyzed the phonetic and spiritual power of divine names</note>, which He has revealed in our faded humanity, in its heavenly part. § 16.

144. Christ intends the "denial" to apply to the soulful mind, so that if anything should exist that might hinder the mind—however beautiful and glorious it may seem in this world—the mind should not regard it, but would rather choose to do without it than lose the love of noble <term>Sophia</term> <note>Greek for Wisdom; Böhme treats Sophia as a personified divine feminine, the "heavenly bride" of the soul</note> in the growth of the flowers of Christ in His tender humanity within us, according to heavenly corporeality. § 29.

### Of True Repentance, Second Book.

145. The more a person goes out from themselves and away from [mental] images, the more they enter into God, until Christ becomes alive in the embodied grace, which happens in the great earnestness of purpose. Thus the marriage with Sophia begins at once, where the two loves receive one another in joy, and with a most inward desire penetrate together into the most sweet love of God; there, in a short time, the wedding of the Lamb is prepared, where the Virgin Sophia (as the worthy humanity of Christ) is wedded to the soul. § 16.

## Second Defense against B. T.

### On the Error of the Sect of Esaias Stiefel and Ezekiel Meth
<note>Esaias Stiefel and his nephew Ezekiel Meth were German mystics who claimed a state of perfection and sinlessness that Böhme argued was impossible while still in the mortal "earthly vessel."</note>

151. The holy power of Jesus and the natural being of the soul are not one in their <term>essence</term> <note>original: "Essenz"</note>; for in Jesus, the <term>source-quality</term> <note>original: "Qual"; Böhme uses this word to signify both "torment" and the "welling up" of a fundamental quality or source-fountain of being.</note> was entirely holy and was God Himself. But in the soul's own property lay the worm of God's ignited wrath, which God intended to kill and extinguish with this holy love flowing from Jesus. Section 489.

152. Christ brought back the virginal state as two <term>tinctures</term> <note>original: "Tincturen"; in Böhme’s alchemy-influenced theology, these are the fundamental spiritual forces (often associated with fire/soul and light/spirit) that must be balanced.</note> in an inseparable, eternal <term>conjunction</term> <note>original: "Conjunction"; a union or marriage of spiritual forces.</note> in love—no longer in the desire for physical substance, as it was in Adam, but united in the desire for spiritual power. These tinctures no longer give birth to physical matter as a form of reproduction, but rather to holy power and the taste of God’s holiness. Section 502.

### Concerning the Last Times, to Paul Kaym, Part I
<note>Paul Kaym was a clothier and self-taught theologian who corresponded with Böhme about the timing of the end of the world and the "thousand-year reign."</note>

153. We must put on the helmet of righteousness and love, and also of chastity and purity, if we wish to go into battle against the prince of this world <note>A biblical reference to Satan.</note>. He cares nothing for outward splendor; only power must overcome him, and that power should shine forth in charity. Thus we can fight for the <term>knight's little wreath</term> <note>original: "Ritter-Kränzlein"; the victor's crown or the prize for spiritual perseverance.</note>; for we have a powerful warrior against us who attacks us in body and soul and strikes us to the ground. He cannot be overcome in any way except with power found in humility; this alone can extinguish his poisonous fire, with which he fights against us and within us against the noble image of God. Section 5.

->The Signature of All Things<-
<note>original: "Signatura Rerum"; one of Jacob Böhme's most influential works (1622), which argues that all physical things are "signatures" or outward signs of inner spiritual realities.</note>

155. A person’s blessedness <note>In Böhme’s context, "Seligkeit" refers to both salvation and the state of eternal joy.</note> lies in this: that he has within himself a true desire for God. For from desire, love wells up; that is, when the desire receives God’s gentleness into itself, the desire sinks into itself within that gentleness and becomes substantial. This then becomes heavenly or Divine essence or corporeality, and within it the soul-spirit (which lay locked in wrath, as if in death) rises again in the love of God: for love <term>tinctures</term> <note>original: "tingiret"; from the alchemical "tincture," meaning to fundamentally transform the inner quality of a substance.</note> death and darkness so that it is once again capable of receiving the radiance of the Divine Sun. Chapter 5, Section 11.

156. The property of nature should be directed simply toward the property of free delight, as toward God’s love-essence, and should direct its hunger toward love. Thus, the hunger receives love into itself and makes it into an essence within itself; then the hunger is no longer a parched, dark hunger that stings and rages within itself like a poisonous <term>Mercury</term> <note>original: "Mercurius"; in Böhme’s alchemy-based philosophy, this represents the restless, driving force of life that can be either "poisonous" (anxious/wrathful) or "vibrant" (joyful) depending on its spiritual orientation.</note>, but instead a love-desire arises out of the hunger. This is called "God’s Nature"; while the hungry, fiery part is called "God’s Wrath"; and in external nature, it is called a fire. Chapter 6, Section 10.

157. The human will must enter with all its strength into Christ’s death and blood, as into the highest <term>tincture</term>. Chapter 11, Section 39.

158. The wrath <note>original: "Grimm"; the fierce, dark, or "sour" quality of God's power when separated from love.</note> which had overwhelmed love in man was to be forgiven; that is, it was to be surrendered into freedom, into the "Nothing," so that it would not be manifest in its own property. It was to become a servant, and only a cause for fiery love and the kingdom of joy. Chapter 11, Section 42.

159. The fire-tincture and light-tincture must become one; the Father’s love and wrath must be only one thing; then that thing is called the Kingdom of Joy. As long as it is divided, there is only anxiety, torment, and vain desire in that thing; but when it burns in a single will, it is an outflowing of joy from itself, and this outgoing property is called the Holy Spirit, as the life of the Godhead. Chapter 11, Section 44.

160. Every life that desires to be without blemish must die in its **will-spirit** to its nature in the fire of <note>original: "Eckels"; Böhme uses "disgust" or "nausea" to describe the soul's turning away from its own dark, selfish roots.</note> disgust at the first impression of wrath; and in its will-spirit toward nature, it must allow itself—as a <term>resigned will</term> <note>original: "gelassener Wille"; a central Böhmean concept referring to the mystical "yielding" or "surrender" (Gelassenheit) to God.</note>—to be led out through death into the light of love, whether it be heavenly or earthly. Thus must it maintain this process, or it will not reach the highest perfection in its degree. Chapter 14, Section 73.

161. The creature in its <term>selfhood</term> <note>original: "Selbheit"; the state of being focused on the "I" or ego, which Böhme considers the root of all evil.</note>, as if in a contentious regime, can neither will nor do anything good; and just as it inflicts nothing but dying and death upon itself, awakening it and making it active, so too can it do nothing else to its fellow members. For from this also originate lies, because the creature denies the unity in the **Will of God** and puts its selfhood in its place, so that it departs from unity into desire and its own lust. If it recognized that all being belongs to the **Mother** <note>In Böhme’s system, "the Mother" refers to the eternal nature or the divine substance from which all things are born.</note> who gave it birth, and if it did not consider the Mother’s being as its own property but as common to all, then greed, envy, strife, and ill-will would not arise—from which anger, as the fire of destruction, emerges. Chapter 15, Section 11.

162. Everything that runs within nature torments itself; but whatever reaches the end of nature is a rest without torment, and yet it still acts, but only in **One Desire**. Chapter 15, Section 52.

### On the Election of Grace.
<note>original: "Von der Gnadenwahl" (1623); Böhme’s major work addressing the controversy of predestination, arguing that God does not arbitrarily choose some for heaven and others for hell, but that humans choose through their own "hunger."</note>

163. From the fiery <term>essence</term> <note>original: "Ente"; a Böhmean term for an entity or the essential substance of a being.</note> of love, the power of fire and light goes out with the spirit upward into the height of the **Tincture** as the "little spirit-water," the name of which is **Virgin Sophia**. <note>In Böhmean mysticism, "Sophia" is the Divine Wisdom or the feminine mirror of God, representing the pure, unfallen humanity.</note> Chapter 3, Section 21.

164. The "little spirit-water" is true humility, which immediately transmutates with the <term>temperature</term> <note>original: "Temperatur"; refers to the perfect balance of the inner qualities, where no single element dominates or "rages."</note> and is drawn back in by the light. For it is the light’s soul according to love, and the fire-soul is the man. Within this lie both **Tinctures**, male and female—the two loves which are Divine in the temperature and were divided in Adam when his imagination turned away from the temperature, but which have been united again in Christ. Chapter 3, Section 22.

165. In the fifth form, the first three forms are no longer painful but full of joy: they draw the tincture of fire and light—namely, Sophia, the greatest gentleness, which is their food.

### The Clavis, or Key.

216. The creation of all things is the revealed, formed Wisdom, which in the human quality <note>original: *Eigenschaft*; a specific characteristic or property of being</note> of the new birth is called Christ. Number 9, Sections 75–79.

217. There are essentially only three properties of nature, according to the revelation of the Holy Trinity of God. As for the 1st: the Desire <note>original: *Begierde*; the primary longing or "contraction" that begins the process of manifestation</note>, which is attributed to God the Father; it is only a spirit, but in the 7th property, the Desire is substantial. The 2nd is attributed to God the Son as the Divine Power; it is only a spirit in the second number, but in the 6th, it is the power of understanding. The 3rd is attributed to God the Holy Spirit according to His revelation; it is only a Fire-Spirit at the beginning of the third property, but in the 5th property, the Great Love is revealed within it. Thus, the outflow of Divine revelation according to the three properties is natural in the First Principle <note>The realm of the "Father," characterized by the fire-source and nature before it meets the Light</note> before the Light, and spiritual in the Second Principle <note>The realm of the "Son," characterized by the Light and the heart of God</note> in the Light. Number 14.

### Theosophical Epistles.

218. God brings no new or foreign spirit into us, but rather He opens our spirit with His Spirit, as the hidden aspect of God’s wisdom that lies within every person, according to the measure and manner of their inner constellation <note>Böhme uses "constellation" to mean the unique spiritual and psychological alignment or makeup of an individual soul</note>. For Christ said: "My Father is working, and I am working too." (John 5:17). Thus the Father works in the essence of the soul-like quality, and the Son works in the essence of God’s image, as in the Divine likeness. Epistle 12, Section 26.

219. The false light originates from the imagination of one’s own natural will, which introduces itself into a government of self-willing by its own power without God’s will; it creates a science <note>original: *Scienz*; meaning a self-derived, intellectual knowledge or "knowingness" that lacks spiritual grounding</note> for itself within itself, and thereby separates itself from God’s will, and is not obedient to the One Will of God outside of nature and creaturely existence. Epistle 47, Section 14.

220. Inquiry must begin from within, in the hunger of the soul. For the inquiry of reason only reaches into its star <note>original: *Astrum*; the governing influence or governing spirit of a particular realm</note> of the outer world, from which reason originates; but the soul inquires into its own star, as into the inner spiritual world, from which the visible world emerged or flowed forth. Epistle 55, Section 4.

## Conclusion of this Supplement.

The growth of the Tincture <term>Tincture: in Böhme’s thought, the spiritual essence or "dye" that transforms and enlivens matter</term> in the Matrix <term>Matrix: the nurturing ground or "womb" of nature and the soul</term> initially manifests in such a way that the spirit—through the dying of the flesh on the ✝ <note>The cross</note> with Christ—returns from the stars <note>original: *Gestirn*; refers to the influence of the physical cosmos or astrological "fate" on the human soul</note> into its internal ground, from which it departed with Adam. He must also, with great struggle, extricate himself from Satan—who is a spirit in the air as if in the abyss—from both below and above. Then, to the earnest warrior, the eternal Word (which became human) appears in the center <note>original: *Centro*</note> of life, and gazes kindly upon the will, which causes the blossoming in the Tincture. Yet, the will still stands only in itself as in selfhood <term>Selbheit: the state of being focused on one's own ego and desires rather than divine will</term>, in the external ground, in the center of the Sun <note>original: *Centro Solis*</note>, and is not yet authentic but rather the son of the bondwoman <note>A biblical reference to Ishmael, son of Hagar, symbolizing the natural man who is not yet the heir of the spiritual promise</note>. Therefore, a deeper birth is still necessary if he wishes to come into God, of which it is said: "we in Him and He in us."

Here, God withdraws Himself from the will once more, so that it may reach a deeper understanding <note>original: *Fassung*; also implies a "containing" or "frame" of mind</note>, whereby the growth within also fades, and from the outside, it becomes the Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil, and is henceforth a pure temptation to the spirit and a trial <note>original: *Proba*</note> to see whether he wishes to remain in the selfhood of his own will, or, with free will, cast himself in obedience into the Word which created him and is his mother (of which Jesus speaks to Nicodemus <note>Referring to the dialogue in John 3 regarding the necessity of being born again</note>), and let God work His way with him; where the will completely "un-becomes" <note>original: *entwird*; a mystical term for the stripping away of the ego and self-attachment</note> in the water of eternal life and becomes thinner than a nothingness. In this state, one leaves it to the Holy Spirit Himself within the hearts of the faithful, how He chooses to reveal Himself, for the vision <note>original: *Schauen*; the gift of mystical contemplation or direct spiritual sight</note> is not granted to all immediately.

# Appendix
## of eight selected epistles of the Author, concerning the approaching Time of the Lily <term>Time of the Lily: Böhme’s term for a prophesied era of peace, spiritual purity, and the "bloom" of divine wisdom before the end of the world</term>, wherein Christ shall rule according to the spirit of heavenly wisdom in the will of love, and the Antichrist <note>To Böhme, the "Antichrist" represented not just a person, but the spirit of institutionalized, loveless religion</note> shall be abolished according to the spirit of this world in the fleshly-wrathful self-will.

### First Letter.
### To Mr. Caspar Lindner, Customs Collector at Beuthen.
### On the Day of Mary’s Assumption, 1621. <note>August 15, 1621</note>

### Summaries.

Wish, § 1. Author is highly delighted over the children of God as his co-branches, 2. 3. recognizes himself as their debtor, 4. in the simple path of a child, 5. wherein he recounts his guidance, 6. and how he was enlightened through many sufferings, 7. and came to the knowledge of the 3 worlds <term>3 Worlds: The Dark world (fire), the Light world (love), and the Outer world (nature)</term>, 8. also was impelled to write, 9. although he struggled with it for 12 years before he could bring it into the external, 10. When the Sun did not shine for him <note>Meaning when he lacked divine inspiration</note>, he did not even know his own work. 11. How his writings became known, 12. and how *Aurora* <note>Böhme’s first book, *Aurora: The Dayspring Dawning*</note> was taken from him? 13. He has written from his own book, which has only 3 leaves <note>Likely referring to the three principles of the divine essence</note>. 14. 15. Often he pleaded with God against his own knowledge, 16. and did not think to become known to people. 17. God dwells in the noble image. 18. All his writing is like that of a schoolboy; 19. the work is God’s. 20. 21. Reason is good and evil; its understanding is from the stars <note>original: *Gestirn*; refers to the influence of the physical cosmos on human intellect</note>. 22. It judges others from without: but the Spirit of God does so from within. 23. The dispute over the letter <note>original: *Buchstaben-Streit*; the conflict over literal interpretations of scripture</note> has grown out of the various gifts of the children of God, 24. for as each one’s soulish spirit is constellated, so is his knowledge. 25. For even the prophets often speak from the external and internal constellation. 30. False reason often also gives false prophets. 31. The center <term>Centrum: the core or heart of a being where spiritual forces originate</term> is the soul: God is the Light. 32. The prophets did not use the same forms. 33. Author will judge no one, 34.

it is written: Those who are led by the Spirit of God are the children of God; and just as one branch on a tree rejoices in the other and gives it its **sap and strength**, so it is also with the children of God in their tree, Jesus Christ. This greatly rejoices my humble person, that God draws us into His wellspring—as simple children to Himself—to our true mother’s breasts, so that we yearn for Him as a child for its mother.

4. Because I then, my beloved lord and brother in the love of Christ, perceive that you carry a thirst for the open fountain of Christ and ask after the fellowship of your brothers, desiring to satisfy yourself in them as a branch in the tree; so it is a pleasure for me to communicate my **sap and spirit**—within the understanding given to me by God—to my brothers and members as my fellow-branches in the tree of Jesus Christ, and to delight myself in them, as in their sap, strength, and spirit. For it is a pleasant food to my soul when I hear how my fellow-branches and members are turning green in the **Paradise of God**.

5. I shall not, however, hide from you the simple child-like path which I walk in Christ. For I cannot write of myself in any other way than as a child who knows and understands nothing, and has never learned anything, except only this: what the Lord wishes to know in me, according to the measure in which He reveals Himself in me.

6. For I never desired to know anything of the **Divine Mystery** <note>Original: "Göttlichen Mysterio"</note>, much less understood how I might seek or find it. I knew nothing of it, as is the **Layman’s way** <note>Böhme emphasizes his status as an uneducated shoemaker—a "layman"—contrasting his direct revelation with the academic study of theologians</note> in its simplicity. I sought only the Heart of Jesus Christ, to hide myself therein from the fierce wrath of God and the assaults of the devil; and I prayed to God earnestly for His Holy Spirit and grace, that He would bless and lead me in Him, and take from me that which turned me away from Him, so that I might surrender myself entirely to Him, so that I might live not to my own will, but to His, and that He alone might lead me, so that I might be His child in His son Jesus Christ.

the gate was opened to me, such that in one quarter-hour I saw and knew more than if I had been many years at the **high schools** <note>Meaning universities or academic institutions.</note>, which I greatly marveled at, not knowing how it happened to me; because of this, I turned my heart to the praise of GOD.

8. For I saw and recognized the **Being of all beings**, the **Ground and the Unground** <term>Ungrund: A central concept in Böhme’s thought, referring to the "bottomless" or "foundationless" abyss of the divine that exists before any created thing.</term>: Also, the birth of the Holy Trinity, the origin and primal state of this world and of all creatures through the Divine Wisdom. I recognized and saw within myself all three worlds: namely (1.) the **Divine, Angelic, or Paradisiacal** world; and then (2.) the **dark world**, as the primal state of Nature leading to fire; and (3.) this **outer, visible world**, as a creature and out-birth, or as an expressed being from the two inner spiritual worlds. I saw and recognized the whole essence in Evil and Good, how one originated from the other, and how the mother of the "birth-giver" was, so that I not only greatly marveled, but also rejoiced.

9. And it struck my mind so strongly that I should write this down for a **Memorial** <note>original: "Memorial" — meaning a record or testimony for future remembrance.</note>: although I could hardly grasp it in my outer man or bring it to the pen; I had to begin working immediately in this very great mystery, like a child going to school. In the interior, I saw it well, as in a great depth, for I saw through it as into a **Chaos** <note>In Böhme's context, "Chaos" refers to the primeval state where all things exist in potential before they are "unfolded" or differentiated.</note>, where everything lies within, but its unfolding was impossible for me.

10. However, it opened itself within me from time to time, as in a growing plant: although I went about with it for 12 years and was pregnant with it in myself, and found a violent drive within me before I could bring it into the **External**: until it later overcame me like a cloudburst—whatever it hits, it hits. So it went with me also: whatever I could grasp to bring into the external, that I wrote down.

11. Although the **Sun** <note>A metaphor for divine inspiration or the "Light of God."</note> shone upon me quite clearly afterwards, it was not always constant. When it hid itself, I could hardly understand my own work; and this happened so that man might recognize that knowledge is not his own, but GOD's—that GOD knows in the soul of man what and how He wills.

<meta>This page continues Jacob Böhme’s account of his early writing years. He describes the confiscation of his first manuscript, *Aurora*, the subsequent period of spiritual darkness and social persecution he endured, and his eventual return to writing with a more refined style and deeper theological insight.</meta>

# First Letter.

12. I intended to keep such writings of mine by me for my entire life and give them to no one. But it happened, by the **Providence of the Most High**, that I entrusted something of them to a certain person, through whom they became public without my prior knowledge. Because of this, my first book (*Aurora*) was taken away from me; and since very wondrous things were revealed therein, which were not quickly comprehensible to the human mind, I had to endure much from those **wise in their own reason** <note>original: "Vernunft-Weisen" — a derisive term Böhme uses for scholars and theologians who relied on intellectual logic rather than spiritual experience.</note>.

13. I did not see that same first book for three years and supposed it was long dead and gone—until copies were sent to me by learned people, exhorting me to reveal my **talent**. Outer reason was nowhere willing to do this, as it had already suffered so much; thus, my reason was very weak and timid. At the same time, the **light of grace** was withdrawn from me for a considerable time, smoldering within me like a hidden fire, so that nothing but anxiety was in me: mockery from without, and a fiery drive from within. Yet I could not grasp it until the Most High came to my aid again with His breath and awakened a new life in me. There, I attained a better **style** <term>Stylum: Böhme refers to his literary and expressive method, which he felt became more sophisticated as his spiritual clarity grew.</term> for writing, as well as a deeper and more grounded knowledge. I could bring everything better into the external, as the book of the *Threefold Life* through the **Three Principles** <term>3 Principia: A central Böhme concept describing three modes of existence: the dark "fire-world" (will), the light "love-world" (spirit), and the visible "outer-world" (nature).</term> now demonstrates, and as the Divine Lover—should his heart be opened to him—will see.

14. Thus I have now written, not from human doctrine or the science of book-learning, but from my own book which was opened within me. As the noble likeness of GOD, the book of the **noble Image** (to be understood as the **image of God**) was granted to me to read; and therein I found my studying, like a child in its mother’s house who sees what the father does and imitates him in its childhood play. I need no other book for this.

15. My book has only three leaves; these are the **Three Principles of Eternity**. Within them, I can find everything that Moses and the prophets, as well as Christ and the Apostles, have spoken. I can [find] the foundation of the world and all **secrets** <note>original: "Heimlichkeit" — referring to the hidden mysteries or inner workings of the divine order.</note> therein

find: Yet not I, but the Spirit of the Lord does it according to the measure as He wills.

16. For I have pleaded with Him many hundreds of times that if my knowledge might not serve His honor and the improvement of my brothers, He would take such things from me and keep me only in His love. But I have found that with my pleading I have only ignited the fire within me more intensely, and in such ignition and knowledge I have produced my *writings*.

17. However, I did not intend to become known among such people as I see now; I still always supposed I was writing for myself. Although the Spirit of God showed me sufficiently in the secrecy of my spirit to what end it was, outer reason was always the *contrary* <note>original: "Contrarium" — Latin for "the opposite" or "opposing force." Böhme often depicts the logical mind as an enemy to spiritual revelation.</note>; except only at times when the *morning star* <note>A significant symbol in Böhme’s work representing the dawning of divine light or the birth of Christ within the soul.</note> arose, then reason was ignited as well and danced along as if it had grasped it, but it is far from it.

18. God dwells in the noble image <note>original: "Bildniß" — referring to the "Image of God" (Imago Dei) within the human being.</note> and not in the astral and elemental spirit; He possesses nothing but Himself in His likeness. And although He indeed possesses something, as He then possesses all things, yet nothing grasps Him except only that which has sprung and come from Him, namely the soul in the likeness of God.

19. Therefore all my writing is like that of a student who goes to school; God has led my soul into a wondrous school, and I can in truth attribute nothing to myself, as if my selfhood <term>Ichheit: Böhme's term for the ego or the individual "I" as distinct from the divine will. He views the "I" as a potential barrier to God.</term> were or understood anything.

20. No one should think more highly of me than what he sees here: for the work in my labor is not mine; I have it only according to the measure as it is granted to me by the Lord; I am only His instrument <term>Werkzeug: literally "tool." Böhme emphasizes that he is a passive vessel for the Holy Spirit.</term> with which He does what He wills. I report this to you, my beloved sir, for your information, so that no one looks for someone else in me who I am not—as one of art and high reason; rather, I live in weakness and childhood, in the simplicity of Christ, in His child-work given to me. In this I have my play, and it is my pastime; in this I have my joy, as in a pleasure garden where many noble flowers stand! With these I will delight myself for a while until I shall again obtain the paradise flowers in the new man.

# First Letter. 295

21. But since, my dear Sir and friend, I see and notice that you also are on this path and seeking, I write to you of my *child-like way* <note>original: "Kinder-Weg" — Böhme's term for the path of spiritual simplicity and humility, contrasting it with the complex intellectualism of scholars.</note> with diligence. For I understand that you make use of various writings, regarding which you desire a **judgment** <note>original: "Judicium" — Latin for a formal opinion or evaluation.</note> from me; this I shall provide to you as my fellow member—as much as **God** has given me to recognize—and that only briefly and in summary. In my book *On the Threefold Life* <note>Referring to his work *The Threefold Life of Man* (1620), which explores the three realms of existence: the divine, the dark/wrathful, and the physical/astral.</note>, you will find it explained extensively according to all circumstances.

22. I give you this, then, as an answer: that one's own reason, which is taught merely from the "letter" <note>Referring to literalist interpretation of scripture without spiritual inspiration.</note> without **God’s** Spirit, blames and despises everything that does not coincide exactly with the laws of the high schools <note>A reference to universities and formal theological academies.</note>. But I marvel at this not at all, for reason is from the outside, and **God’s** Spirit is from within; reason is both good and evil, it travels along like a wind and allows itself to be weighed and driven; it pays heed to human judgment, and whatever the high reputation of this world judges, it judges accordingly as well. It does not recognize the **Lord’s** mind, for He is not in it: Its understanding is from the stars <note>original: "Gestirne" — In Böhme's cosmology, the "astral" or "starry" spirit governs the physical mind and worldly logic, but cannot grasp the divine.</note>, and is only a mirror over against Divine Wisdom.

23. How may one judge divine things in whom the Spirit of the **Lord** is not? The Spirit of the **Lord** alone tests and judges all things; for to Him alone is everything known and revealed. Reason, however, judges from the outside, and one reason always judges according to another: the small according to the great, the layman according to the doctor <note>In Böhme’s time, "Doctor" referred to a high-ranking academic or theologian.</note>, and no one grasps the truth and the **Lord’s** mind, except the Spirit of **God**, who judges within the human being and has no respect for persons; the layman is to Him the same as the doctor.

24. But that the children of **God** have such various gifts for writing, speaking, and judging, and do not all use the same *style* <note>original: "Stylum" — Latin for literary style or manner of expression.</note>—from which one's own reason later sucks out its own benefit and creates a Babel <note>A reference to the Tower of Babel, symbolizing the confusion of tongues and the sectarian strife between different religious factions.</note>, from which so many kinds of opinions have arisen—it has come to pass that people have devised opinions and "ways to **God**" from their writings, which ways people were supposed to walk: and thus such a quarrel has arisen that now man looks only at the strife, seeing who can overcome the other with the exchange of letters. This is all Babel, a mother of spiritual harlotry <note>original: "geistliche Hurerey" — A common Reformation-era term for religious idolatry or the corruption of the soul by following false systems instead of Christ.</note>, where reason does not enter through the door of **Christ**, by **Christ’s** Spirit into the

28. Thus the Spirit of Christ now opens to every soul its own property, so that each speaks from its own property of the wonders in the wisdom of **God**.

<meta>This page continues Böhme's explanation of how spiritual knowledge arises from the "inner constellation" of the soul. # First Letter. 297

spirit of the outer world. It opens within man the inner soulful constellation <note>Referring to the spiritual alignment or "makeup" of the soul, as described on the previous page.</note>, so that he must prophesy what the outer heaven works. Likewise, he must speak through the Great Turmoil <note>original: "Turbam magnam" — in Böhme's thought, the *Turba* is the "Great Disturbance" or the power of divine wrath and judgment that breaks apart things that have fallen into sin.</note>, as the prophets often spoke and indicated to the people the punishment which should befall them through the Great Turmoil, by **God's** decree, for the sake of their sins.

30. Thus the Spirit of **God** often speaks in one person through the inner eternal constellation of the soul, concerning eternal punishment or reward; and another speaks through the (outer) constellation, concerning the fortune and misfortune of this world, the rise of all power, and also the destruction of lands and cities; likewise, concerning the marvelous transformation of the world.

31. And although it is true that the spirit of the outer world also often plays its game in man, and by its own power sights itself into the human spirit and indicates its strange figure—as happens with those who run merely in reason and in proud self-will, from which false prophets often arise—therefore I say now, that everyone speaks from his constellation: one through the revelation of the Spirit of **God** truthfully, the other through the opening of the outer star-spirit uncertainly, yet each speaks from that same constellation. But he who speaks of the mystery from another’s mouth and judges without his own knowledge, that is Babel <note>Böhme uses "Babel" to represent the "tower" of human-made, confused religious systems built on intellectual pride rather than direct spiritual revelation.</note> and delusion, a thing that the heart does not experience as to whether it be true.

32. And I say further, that all those precious men enlightened by **God**, whose writings you may partly have in your hands, have spoken from their own opening, each according to his own concept. 34. These aforementioned authors <note>original: "Autores"</note>, about whom you desire my opinion, I have not read in full, but in part. I have no wish to judge them—far be it from me—even if they did not all possess a single style of writing. For knowledge is of many kinds; yet it is my part, through my own gifts, to test their hearts and wills. When I find, however, that their hearts and spirit spring from one Center <note>original: "Centro"</note>, as from the Spirit of Christ, I am content with the Center, and I leave the speaking of the highest tongues to the Spirit of God’s wisdom, who reveals it to everyone through wisdom in the measure He wills.

35. I judge no one, and condemnation is but false chatter. The Spirit of **God** Himself judges all things; if that same Spirit is in us, why then should we inquire so long after mere chatter? Rather, I rejoice much more in the gifts of my brothers. If it happens that they have a different gift of expression than I, should I judge them for that?

36. Does one herb, flower, or tree say to another: "You are sour and dark; I do not wish to stand beside you"? Do they not all have one mother from which they grow? So too do all souls come from one, and all people from one. Why then do we boast of being children of **God** when we are more foolish than the flowers and the herbs of the field? Is it not also the case with us that **God** reveals His wisdom within us? Just as He reveals the <term>tincture of hiddenness</term> <note>In Böhme's alchemy-influenced thought, a "tincture" is a vitalizing spiritual essence that transforms and brings forth life and color from the "hidden" or inner realm of nature.</note> in the earth, through the earth with beautiful plants, so also does He in us humans. We should much rather rejoice in this and love one another heartily, that **God** reveals His wisdom in us in such manifold ways. But he who judges and condemns in a godless way, running only in pride to make himself seen, is a driver of Babel <note>Referring to the "Tower of Babel"—for Böhme, a symbol of the confused, prideful, and divided state of institutional religion and human intellect.</note> and a turning wheel that only stirs up strife.

The true and simple way to come to **God** is this, as much as I am able to recognize it: Namely, that a person should depart from the sins they have committed and make a serious resolution never to enter into them again, and in this departing, they should not doubt.

38. And although reason <note>original: "Vernunft"; Böhme often uses this to mean human logic that is disconnected from divine insight.</note> certainly doubts, which causes the sinner to be startled and terrified by the wrath of **God**, let the will simply and truly sink itself into the mercy of **God**, into Christ’s suffering and death, and surrender itself through Christ into **God**—like a child in its mother’s lap, who wants nothing of itself except what the mother wants. It only cries out to the mother and always hopes for the best from the mother, longing only for the mother’s breasts. In the same way, our desire must be simply redirected back into our first mother, from whom we departed with Adam into a "selfhood" <note>original: "Eigenes"; refers to the ego or self-will that separates the soul from God.</note>.

39. Therefore Christ says: *Unless you turn and become like children, you shall not see the kingdom of **God**.* Matthew 18:3. Also: *You must be born again.* John 3:7. That is, we must go out of all reason and back into <term>yieldedness</term> <note>original: "Gelassenheit"; a core concept in German mysticism meaning total surrender of the self-will to God.</note>, into our mother's lap, and let all disputing go. We must make our reason entirely as if dead, so that the Mother-Spirit may take a form within us and breathe the Divine Life into us, so that we find ourselves in the Mother-Spirit as if in a cradle, if we wish to be taught and driven by **God**.

40. We must yield ourselves entirely to Him, so that **God’s** Spirit may be the willing, the doing, and the accomplishing within us—so that we may know Him and not ourselves, and so that He may be our knowledge.

41. We should by no means say what we want to know; rather, we should merely enter into the Incarnation <note>original: "Menschwerdung"</note> and birth of **Jesus Christ**, into His suffering and death, and always be willing to walk in His footsteps and follow Him. We must remember that we are on the Pilgrim’s Road, where we must travel through a dangerous path back into our fatherland (from which Adam led us) by entering again in Christ upon the narrow path. On this single way lies the <term>Great Mystery</term> <note>original: "Perlein Mysterium Magnum"; literally "the Pearl of the Great Mystery."</note>. All studying, seeking, and searching outside of this way is dead and achieves nothing.

The 2nd part is extremely deep, concerning **Christ’s suffering and death**; how we must enter into Christ’s death, die and rise again with and in Christ. And why Christ had to die; explained entirely from the **Center** <note>original: "Centro"; the spiritual point of origin from which all life and nature spring.</note> through the Three Principles—very profound. The 3rd part is the **Tree of the Christian Faith**, also explained through the Three Principles; very useful to read.

71. VI. The 6th book or part of these writings consists of **six (theosophical) points** of the greatest depth: how the Three Principles beget each other and relate to one another, so that in eternity there is no conflict, and each is truly within itself. And from whence conflict and disharmony arise; the origin of good and evil; introduced entirely from the **Abyss** <note>original: "Ungrund"; Böhme's famous term for the "Groundless" or the primordial nothingness out of which the divine will and all existence emerge.</note>, as if from nothing into something, as into the foundation of nature. This 6th book is such a mystery—though expressed in a childlike way—that no reason will grasp its foundation without the **Light of GOD**. It is a key to the **Alpha and Omega (to Everything)** <note>original: "A und O (Allem)"</note>.

One fights over the husks <note>Böhme often uses the metaphor of "husks" (Hülsen) to describe external religious dogmas or rituals that lack the living spiritual "juice" or essence.</note>, and the noble juice, which serves for life, is left standing.

62. What does **knowledge** <note>original: "Wissenschaft"; in this era, the term refers to systematic learning or theological study rather than modern laboratory science.</note> profit me if I do not live within it? Knowledge must be in me, as well as the will and the deed. The cloak of the suffering and **satisfaction of Christ**, which is now draped over people, will become a snare and hellish fire to many, in that they only wish to tickle themselves with Christ’s satisfaction while keeping the **rogue** <note>original: "Schalk"; Böhme uses this term to describe the unregenerate "old man" or the sinful ego that hides behind outward piety.</note> within.

63. It is said: *You must be born again, or you shall not behold the **Kingdom of GOD**; you must become as a child if you wish to see the Kingdom of GOD.* One should not merely wrangle over knowledge, but become a new person who lives in righteousness and holiness in GOD. One must drive out the rogue and put on Christ; then we are in Christ, and buried with Christ in His death, and rise with Christ, and live eternally in Him. Why then should I wrangle for long over that which I myself am?

64. I have no quarrel with anyone, except only against the godless, whom the Spirit rebukes to their face: I would not wish to hide this from you, and I mean it faithfully.

65. Concerning my books, you can, as I have heard, easily obtain them for yourself if they please you; for Mr. **Christian Bernhard**, the tax collector at Sagan, informs me how he has two of them (namely the one on the **Threefold Life** <note>The Threefold Life of Man (1620), one of Böhme's core works.</note>, which is almost the most principal in teaching, and then the **40 Questions on the Soul**), which he has lent to your wine-steward’s brother. You can befriend him, and he will not refuse them to you. If not, however, I will help you to them in other ways; you can also get them from Mr. Christian Bernhard if you ever desire them and can no longer find them; I will write to him that he should lend them to you, for I rarely have my own at home. However, if you should not obtain them, I would, as soon as I got them back home, lend them to you one after the other.

66. Their titles and the different books are these: I. The **Aurora**, which rises out of childhood <note>Böhme refers to *Aurora* (1612) as his "childhood" work because it was his first, written in a state of initial, unrefined revelation.</note> and shows you the creation of all beings, but almost in secret and not clearly enough. It explains much **Magical Understanding**, for there are several mysteries within it that are yet to come to pass.

67. II. A large book of 100 sheets <note>original: "Bogen"; referring to the large sheets of paper used in binding manuscripts, indicating a very substantial volume.</note>, regarding the **Three Principles of Divine Essence**, and of the Essence of All Essences: This is a key and an alphabet for all those who desire to understand my writings. It treats of Creation; likewise, of the eternal birth of the Deity; of repentance, the justification of man, and his life in Paradise, and of the Fall. Likewise: of the new birth, and Christ’s Testaments, and of the whole of human salvation; it is very useful to read, for it is an eye to recognize the wonders in the **Mystery of GOD**.

68. III. A book of the **Threefold Life**, consisting of 60 sheets; it is a key from above and below to all secrets, wherever the heart might wish to soar. It shows the entire ground of the Three Principles and serves everyone according to their own nature: one may find the basis for almost all questions that reason can devise within it. And it is the most necessary thing that could well serve you; you would soon grow weary of the **polemical books** <note>original: "Zank-Bücher"; referring to the aggressive religious arguments and sectarian pamphlets common during the Reformation and Counter-Reformation.</note>, if you took this into your soul.

69. IV. **40 Questions on the Soul**, consisting of 28 sheets, dealing with everything that a person ought to know.

70. The V. Book has 3 parts. The 1st part is on the **Incarnation of Christ**. The 2nd part is very deep indeed, concerning Christ’s suffering and death; how we must enter into Christ’s death, to die and rise again with and in Christ: and why Christ had to die; explained entirely from the **Center** <note>original: "Centro"; Böhme uses this to refer to the inner spiritual core or origin point of existence.</note> through the Three Principles, very profound. The 3rd part is the **Tree of Christian Faith**, also explained through the Three Principles, very useful to read.

71. VI. The 6th book or part of these writings consists of **6 (Theosophic) Points** of the very greatest depth: how the Three Principles beget each other and harmonize, so that in eternity there is no strife, and each is truly within itself; and from whence strife and discord come; from whence evil and good originate; traced entirely out of the <term>Ungrund (the Groundless)</term> <note>Böhme’s term for the absolute nothingness or the "abyss" that precedes even God’s self-manifestation.</note>, as from Nothing into Something, and into the ground of Nature. This 6th book is such a mystery—though expressed in a childlike way—that no reason will grasp its ground without the light of GOD. It is a key to **Alpha and Omega** (to All).

72. VII. A small booklet for **Melancholy**, for the

# First Letter.

...written for the afflicted: from where sadness originates, and how one should resist it (this is from the **Four Complexions** <term>Complexions: Referring to the four temperaments—sanguine, choleric, melancholic, and phlegmatic—which were believed to govern human health and personality.</term> No. IX. *Christosophia* No. 8).

73. VIII. A very deep book, *On the Signature of All Things* <term>Signatura Rerum: Böhme’s doctrine that every object in the natural world bears a "signature" or physical mark that reveals its inner spiritual essence.</term> Concerning the designation of Creation, and what the beginning, as well as the breaking and healing, of every thing might be; it proceeds entirely into the Eternal, and then into the original external Nature and its configurations.

74. These, then, are my books, alongside several small little treatises that I have given away here and there, of which I have kept no copy, for I have no need of them for myself; I have enough in my "three leaves" <note>The "three leaves" or "three pages" is a recurring metaphor for Böhme’s primary revelation of the three principles: the dark world, the light world, and the external world.</note>.

75. And as my opportunity allows—for I must otherwise often travel because of my work—I will speak with you in person as soon as I may be traveling through these parts. I intended to do so when I was in Weicha after Easter; that was my whole purpose, but GOD turned it otherwise, sending me a man who led me along other paths to such people where it was necessary, so that I recognized afterward that my way was from the LORD.

76. Mr. Balthasar Walter <note>A physician and chemist who traveled extensively in search of ancient wisdom; he was one of Böhme’s most important early supporters and helped systematize his terminology.</note> stayed this past winter and spring with Prince Augustus of Anhalt, etc., at Pless, and wrote to me from there. Currently, he is with the Count of Gleichen, three miles from Erfurt; he has been appointed as his physician for one year.

77. At the same court is also Ezechiel Meth <note>A leader of a radical spiritualist movement in Germany who, along with his brother-in-law Esaias Stiefel, claimed a form of perfection that Böhme eventually found problematic.</note>, but they are not entirely of one mind, as Walter's letter shows, which I only received three weeks ago. If you, sir, should wish to write anything to me and have no messenger coming here, you may simply send it to Mr. Christian Bernhard, the customs official at Sagan; I have opportunity there every week, for he is a God-fearing fellow.

78. Should anything in my writings be too difficult or incomprehensible, please just make a note of it; I wish to present it in a childlike way <note>original: "kindisch"; in Böhme's time, this often meant "simple" or "straightforward," like a father speaking to a child, rather than the modern negative sense of "childish."</note> so that it may be understood. To the clever and the sated, the high and the self-wise, who can walk by themselves and are already rich—to those I have written nothing, but rather to the children and the babes who suck at their mother's breasts and are learning to walk.

79. Whoever can understand it, let them understand it; but whoever cannot,

## Second Letter.

->To Mr. Gottfried Freudenhammer, of<-
->Freudenheim, Doctor of Medicine at Großen-Glogau.<-
->From October 17, 1621.<-

### Summaries.

The Greeting. §. 1. 2. The book in which all mystery lies is man himself. 3. From the lily-twig <term>Lily-twig: Böhme’s symbol for the spiritual flowering of the soul and the dawning of a new age of the Holy Spirit.</term> the Holy Spirit grows green, 4. and that same twig is the newborn spirit. 5. 6. One born from within inherits God’s kingdom: no stranger, 7. nor anything earthly. 8. The 5th essence <term>Quinta Essentia: The "quintessence" or highest spiritual element that transcends the four physical elements (earth, air, fire, water).</term> must rule over the 4 elements. 9. The outer world rules over the outer man. 10. Therefore he must die. 11. Through the struggle, the Mystery becomes manifest, 12. 13. and the light is born again, 14. when God’s love penetrates the soul through grace. 15. Therefore, the doctrine of "imputed righteousness" <note>Referring to the theological debate where Böhme argued that righteousness must be an internal reality (regeneration), not just a legal status granted by God.</note> is a groundless concept. 16. 17. We must kill the old Adam <note>The "old Adam" refers to the fallen, sinful nature of humanity.</note> with God’s love. 18. God’s kingdom must be born in us, 19. and we must enter it through Christ. 20. For reason does not create a child of God; 21. likewise, the "I-ness" <note>Self-centered ego or "Ichheit."</note> cannot reach it. 22. The earthly will must die, 23. and cling to God’s mercy. 24. In this mercy, man rises, 25. and dwells in heaven, in the new man. 26. In this way, the Author found the Mystery, 27. which God has made known to others, 28. according to the prophecy of Joel (Chapter 3:1). 29. 30. He thereby recommends humility, 31. and warns against the starry heaven <note>The "astral" or "starry" influence, which Böhme believed could distract from purely spiritual growth.</note>, 32. by which even the Methists <term>Methists: Likely Böhme's term for those focused on intellectual or mathematical calculations—"Mathists"—rather than spiritual experience.</term> were seized again. 33. May the small sown grain remain in the highest humility before God until it has grown into a tree, 34. from whose blossom the Morning Star rises. 35. The 7th angel has prepared his trumpet; whereupon the strict judgment follows upon Babel <note>Babel: Böhme's common term for the "confused" and corrupt institutional churches of his time.</note>. 36.

->**May the open fountain of GOD in the heart of Jesus Christ,**<-

**Honorable**, Respected and Highly Learned Sir; I wish for the Sir, solely and alone, what my soul desires from **GOD**, namely the right, true, **Divine** knowledge in the love of **JESUS CHRIST**, so that **GOD** might unlock the <term>Centrum</term> <note>Latin: "center." In Böhme's thought, the "center" is the point of origin within the soul where the divine light or the dark fire emerges.</note> of his soul. Thus the Paradisiacal Lily-twig might grow green, flourish, bloom and bear fruit in **Christ's** rose-garden, and the stream from **Christ's** fountain might flow out from him, and he may be taught by **GOD**, so that His **Holy Spirit** alone may drive and govern him, as it is written: Those who are led by the Spirit of **GOD** are the children of **GOD**.

2. I have received the Sir's letter and understood from it that he has read my writings and found pleasure in them; I wish from the heart that their sense and right understanding may be grasped, for then he would need no further questioning or searching.

3. For the book in which all secrets lie within is man himself: He is himself the book of the essence of all essences, since he is the likeness of the Godhead; the great <term>Arcanum</term> <note>Latin: "secret" or "mystery." In alchemy and mysticism, it refers to the hidden, fundamental essence of reality.</note> lies within him, yet the revelation belongs to the Spirit of **GOD**.

4. But if the love-(lilies) in **Christ's** humanity green forth from the soul in the new rebirth, then the Spirit of **GOD** goes out from those same lilies as from its own origin and ground; that same Spirit seeks and finds all hidden things in **Divine** wisdom.

5. For the Lily-twig, which greens forth in the new birth from **Christ's** humanity (understand: the newborn spirit, from the soul's <term>Essence</term>, in **Christ's** power), is a true branch standing out from and within **GOD’S** tree.

6. Just as a mother gives birth to a child, so the new man is born in and out of **GOD**; in this way and in no other is he **GOD’S** child and heir, a child of heaven and paradise.

7. For it is not an imputed righteousness <note>A reference to the theological concept of "forensic justification," where God "counts" a person as righteous. Böhme argues instead for an "essential" or "inborn" righteousness that actually transforms the person's nature.</note> that counts—a stranger cannot inherit **GOD’S** kingdom—but rather an inborn righteousness from **GOD’S** essence, as from **GOD**—

...[born of] water and Spirit, as Christ tells us: We must become as children, and be received into **God’s Essence** <note>original: "Gottes Essenz." For Böhme, "essence" refers to the underlying spiritual substance or "being-ness" of God that forms the foundation of all reality.</note>, and green forth and be born out of **God’s Essence** as new children, in the same way that a beautiful flower grows out of the wild earth, or as a precious, beautiful gold grows in the coarse stone; otherwise, we can neither behold nor inherit God’s kingdom.

8. For that which wishes to inherit the inner **Spiritual World** must be born from the same: The earthly flesh from the **4 elements** <note>The traditional classical elements: earth, air, fire, and water, which Böhme associates with the temporary, physical world.</note> cannot inherit God’s kingdom. John 6:63. I Cor. 15:50.

9. The fifth essence, however, as the **Holy Element**, from which the **4 elements** are born (that is, **Paradise**), that must rule over the **4 elements**, in the same way that the light holds the darkness within itself, as if swallowed up, even though the darkness is truly within it; thus must it also be with man.

10. Only, during this time of earthly life, it cannot be so with the outer man; for the outer world rules over the outer man, because it was made manifest in Adam, which is his fall.

11. Therefore, the outer man must break apart, just as the outer world breaks apart, and for this reason, perfection cannot be reached by a man in this [current] time; rather, the true man must remain in struggle against the earthly, corrupted life, which is his opposite, where eternity and time struggle against one another.

12. For through the struggle, the great <term>Arcanum</term> <note>Latin: "secret" or "mystery." In alchemy and Böhme's thought, it is the hidden spiritual core or the "elixir" of life.</note> is opened, and the eternal wonders in God’s wisdom are made manifest out of the soulful essence.

13. Just as the eternal God has revealed Himself with time, and leads His eternal wonders into struggle and adversity with time—so that through the struggle that which is hidden may open itself—so also must the great <term>Mysterium</term> <note>Latin: "mystery." Here referring to the *Mysterium Magnum*, the chaos or "great mystery" from which all things were created.</note> in man be made manifest in the struggle, where God’s wrath and love are in conflict, just as fire and light are in conflict.

14. For in the **Souls** (which originate from the eternal fire, from the Father’s property, as from the eternal, beginning-less nature, out of the darkness) the light—which was extinguished in Adam—must again [be born] in Christ's inspiration...

[...to be] born, then Christ and **God’s Kingdom** are given to him out of grace.

15. Then no human can take that from him; **God’s Love** penetrates through grace back into the **Center of the Soul**, and leads the will of God into heavenly essence <note>original: "Wesenheit." For Böhme, this is the substantial reality of the spiritual world.</note>, as a new branch, or a new image out of the **Soul-Fire** <note>Böhme viewed the soul as a "fire" that is either a painful burning of self-will or, when illuminated by God, a light-giving warmth.</note>, just as the light shines out from the fire.

16. Therefore it is all **baseless** <note>original: "Ungrund." While Böhme often uses this term to describe the "Abyss" of God, here he uses it to mean "without foundation" or "groundless nonsense."</note>, what **Babel** <note>Böhme uses "Babel" to refer to the confused, institutionalized churches of his day, which he believed focused on external rules rather than internal transformation.</note> teaches concerning external imputed righteousness and an externally accepted sonship; Christ spoke: *You must be born anew, otherwise you shall not see God’s Kingdom.* John 3:3.

17. It helps nothing to offer hypocritical comforting with Christ’s death; rather, one must enter into **Christ’s death**, and **green forth** <note>original: "ausgrünen." A favorite botanical metaphor of Böhme’s, suggesting a natural, living growth of the spirit like a plant blooming.</note> in Him, rise in Him and with Him, and become the **new man** in Christ.

18. Just as Christ—with His love, as with the newly-introduced **Love-Fire**—has killed, extinguished, and overcome the world, and also His Father’s wrath as the Center of eternal nature in the Soul-property, into the **Soul-Essence** (into which previously the devil had introduced his desire); so must we, in and with Christ’s Spirit, drown the **earthly Adam** in God’s wrath, and kill it with God’s love, so that the new man greens forth. Otherwise there is no forgiveness of sins, nor sonship, nor righteousness.

19. The **Kingdom of God** must be born within us, otherwise we cannot see with the eye of eternity into the **Angelic world**.

20. All poeticizing and striving, learning and studying is in vain; neither art nor reason achieves it. We must only enter through the door that God has opened for us in Christ, and **green forth** in God’s Kingdom, and die to the earthly will, so that it only hangs on behind us; the **seed of the woman** must forever crush the serpent's head within us.

21. **Self-Reason** <note>original: "Eigen-Vernunft." Human logic or cleverness divorced from spiritual divine guidance.</note> cannot make a child of God, for it does not depend on our willing, running, and racing, as Paul says; but on God’s mercy. Romans 9:16.

22. My **selfhood** <note>original: "Ichheit." Böhme uses this to describe the ego or the self-centered nature that separates humans from God.</note> cannot achieve it; my selfhood must die in Christ’s death and fall back into the Nothing. Then my selfhood falls into God’s mercy and reaches the goal of the first man, standing again in the **Creative Word** <note>original: "Verbo Fiat." Latin for "the Word: Let it be," referring to God's creative power in Genesis.</note>. There, God’s mercy—through Christ’s entry into our humanity—makes the new man out of grace.

23. Therefore, the corrupted, earthly will must die through right, true repentance and enter into **yieldedness** <term>Gelassenheit: a central term in German mysticism meaning a state of complete surrender, letting go of self-will to allow God to act through the soul</term>, as into the Nothing. It must entirely surrender the will of its reason to death and no longer want or know itself, but hang upon God’s mercy.

24. Then it is said, as God speaks through the prophet:
> My heart breaks for him, that I must have mercy on him. Can a mother also forget her child, that she should not have mercy on the son of her womb? And even if she should forget, yet I will not forget you; behold, I have engraved you in my hands.

25. In this, as in God’s mercy, the new man arises and **grows green** <note>original: "grünet." Böhme frequently uses botanical metaphors to describe spiritual growth.</note> in the Kingdom of Heaven and Paradise, even though the earthly body (the man) is in this world.

26. For St. Paul says:
> Our citizenship is in heaven.
Phil. 3:20. Thus the new man walks in heaven, and the old man in this world; for the heaven where God dwells is within the new man.

27. Thus, my beloved lord and brother, and in no other way, have I found the **Mystery** <note>original: "Mysterium."</note>; I have not studied or learned it. If you or another thirst for it, I am brotherly inclined to show the way, just as it occurred to me and as I have written at length in my writings—especially in the book *Of the Threefold Life of Man* and in the book *Of the Three Principles of Divine Essence*.

28. Truly, I wrote for myself as a spiritual exercise in the **knowledge of God** <note>original: "Erkenntniß GOttes."</note> and in the Mystery of God's great wonders. But because it has come to be read through God’s providence, I grant it to everyone who earnestly desires to understand it. I wish from my heart that it might be revealed and known within the reader themselves, for then no further searching would be needed.

29. Because God has promised through the prophets—especially in Joel 3:1—that He will pour out His Spirit in the last time upon all flesh, this time must be carefully observed. <note>original: Joel 3:1. In many German Bibles of the time, this refers to the passage known in modern English Bibles as Joel 2:28: "I will pour out my Spirit on all people."</note>

30. I say, as I have recognized it: Whoever is willing to die to themselves right now, the Spirit of the Lord—according to Joel’s interpretation—wants to seize them and reveal His wonders through them. Therefore, if someone is in earnest, they will experience it.

31. But I want everyone to be faithfully warned: should it happen that God’s light rises within them, they must remain standing in great humility in **yieldedness** <term>Gelassenheit: a state of total surrender to God's will, setting aside the ego</term>, as if in the death of Christ.

32. For heaven shall now pour out its long-wrought **outflow** <note>original: "Egest." From the Latin *egestio*, referring to a discharge or byproduct. Böhme uses it to describe the influence or "sediment" deposited by the stars into human nature.</note> from the stars, which it co-produced in human nature; this is so that the person is not seized by the starry heaven <note>The "starry heaven" in Böhme's thought represents the physical, astrological, and psychological influences of the material universe that can distract the soul from God.</note> and does not rush out beyond the goal, leaving the state of yieldedness.

33. As can be seen in the **Enthusiasts** <note>original: "Methisten." This likely refers to "Metists" or other "spiritualist" sects of the time who Böhme believed claimed spiritual perfection too quickly or falsely.</note>, who reached the very gates of the Deep, but were seized again by the starry heaven. They entered back into themselves, became prideful, and left the struggle against the **Serpent** <note>The "Serpent" represents the deceptive, self-centered nature of the ego and the devil.</note>; thus they entered into a selfhood of their own, imagining they were entirely **transmuted** <note>original: "transmutiret." An alchemical term for changing one substance into another, here meaning transformed into God's essence.</note> into God, and so they mixed the outer world with the inner world.

34. This is a **lack of foundation** <note>original: "Ungrund." While Böhme often uses "Ungrund" to mean the divine "Abyss" or "Great Mystery," here he uses it to denote a "bottomless error" or a state without a proper spiritual base.</note>, and one must take great care to remain standing in the highest humility before God, until a tree grows from the small sown seed and comes to blossom, and the Spirit of God gains a form within them.

35. For from the blossom, the **Morning Star** rises, so that the person learns to know themselves—what they are, and what God and Time are.

36. I inform the Lord with good intentions that the present time is to be carefully observed, for the seventh angel in the **Revelation** <note>original: "Apocalypsi." Referring to the Book of Revelation 11:15, where the seventh trumpet announces the kingdom of the world becoming the kingdom of God.</note> has prepared his trumpet. The powers of heaven are in a singular motion; additionally, both doors are open—Light and Darkness—and in great desire. As each person is seized, so shall they enter in; whatever one greatly rejoices in, that will...

## Third Letter.
->To N. N.<-
->Dated November 1, 1622.<-

## On the Killing of the Antichrist within Ourselves.

### Summary.

The author's offering of brotherly love. §. 1. The Antichrist holds the rule in Christendom. 2. Christ teaches self-denial—namely, that man should leave the Antichrist, as **mine-ness** <term>Meinheit: a Böhmean term for egoism or the grasping sense of "me and mine"</term>, 3. and go out from all **selfhood** <term>Eigenheit: the state of being driven by one's own ego or self-will instead of God's will</term>, 4. even if he were a king. 5. He should lead his soul's will into the sonship of God, 6. and baptize it into God's mercy, 7. and also stand firm and fight in the promise of grace; ibid. whereby the soul becomes a young child. 8. Adam departed from **concordance** <term>Concordanz: a state of inner harmony or being in "one accord" with God's will</term> and fell prey to death. 9. 10. Out of this death, Christ rises in His spirit; ibid. and in this renewal the spirit comes to **contemplation** <term>Schaulicheit: the state where the spiritual reality becomes visible or perceptible to the soul's inner eye</term>, 11. and is like pure gold in the coarse stone. 12. In our supposed religion, we are stuck in the middle of Babylon. 13. The adopted purple mantle covers the Antichrist, 14. and hypocritically conceals the self-will. 15. Only those who go out from selfhood obtain the **pearl** <note>A reference to the "Pearl of Great Price" (Matthew 13:46), symbolizing the divine spark or Christ-nature within</note>, 16. and no one can take comfort in the merit of Christ except he who has **put on Christ**, 17. whose beginning occurs in baptism. 18. Therefore a Christian must be born from Christ, 19. and God's Spirit must possess Christ's temple. 20. No animal can eat Christ's flesh, 21. but only he who has put on Christ. 22. One must consider **reason** <note>original: "Vernunft." Böhme often contrasts human logical reason with divine "Understanding" (Verstand)</note> to be foolish; 23. for the **wisdom of the world** is blind toward God. 24. All of which the author has explained quite centrally in his writings. 25. sq.

## Our Salvation in Christ Jesus.

Honorable, well-named Sir; I wish you, through God in Christ Jesus, His grace, knowledge, and blessing. Since I have been informed by Doctor R. R. <note>likely referring to Balthasar Walther, a physician and Böhme's mentor</note> how the Sir, as a Christian fellow-brother in the Lord, stands in the "drawing of the Father" toward Christ Jesus in heartfelt desire, and labors in his mind toward that end...

He should baptize himself entirely into the deepest lowliness and unworthiness before God with **penitence** <term>Pönitenz: from the Latin *poenitentia*, meaning the internal act of contrition and the external discipline of repentance</term>, but in the soul, he must grasp the promise of grace and stand therein as a **soldier** before his enemy, when it is a matter of body and life.

8. When this happens, his own will—acting as the **Antichrist**—is seized and killed in the death of Christ. Immediately, his soul begins to stand before God as a **new, simple child** <note>original: "unverständiges Kind," meaning a child without the complex, deceptive reasoning of the adult ego</note> that has lost its natural understanding of **selfhood** <term>Selbheit: the state of being focused on the self</term>. It stands like a young child before its mother and places its trust in the mother for whatever she wishes to give it.
