# Fourth Letter.
## To Mr. N. N.
### On the Day of Christ’s Entry <note>Palm Sunday, commemorating Christ’s entry into Jerusalem.</note>, 1623.
### Summaries.

Only in Divine mercy and compassion can one recognize their own condition and temptation. §. 1. 2. Temptations arise from **Self-love**, which stands against the love of GOD; 3. and from one’s own nature, into which the Devil shoots his false desire; 4. this temptation is the greatest, and is precisely the struggle of Christ within us; 5. which struggle we would not have if the love of GOD in Christ had not been infused into us. 6. Thus, however, the struggle arises quite perceptibly from the **Dragon** <note>Böhme’s term for the prideful, unregenerate ego or the devilish influence within the soul.</note>; 7. because Christ storms his **robber-castle** <term>robber-castle: a "stronghold" or defensive position of the ego and sinful nature within the soul.</term>; 8. and treads upon the serpent’s head; 9. and the soul stands in the desert. 10. The second temptation from the Dragon of one's own nature is that once the soul is enlightened, it wants to possess that same light as its own property. 11. Nature of the Dragon, 12. and the false speaking of Reason. 12. 13. Nature must die to its own will; from this come the trials; and no godless person feels this struggle. 14 15. If Christ is now to live, then the **spirit of self-pleasure** must die. ibid. The third temptation stands in the will and the mind, also in flesh and blood, as in the Devil's robber-castles. 16. Now let everyone examine what their temptation might be? 17. All temptation is within **selfhood** <note>original: "Eigenheit." The state of being focused on the "I" or "Self" rather than God.</note>. 18. Christian counsel against it. 19. Christ himself fights for our soul. 20. If we let all earthly will go and surrender ourselves to Him entirely, then with Christ we become **knights** <note>or champions</note> over all our enemies. 21.

### Our Salvation in the Life of JESUS Christ within us!

**M**uch beloved Lord and fellow-member brother <note>original: "gliederlicher Mitbruder." Refers to being a fellow "limb" or "member" of the mystical Body of Christ.</note> in Christ our Savior; along with my heartfelt wishes and a participating desire for Divine love and grace; I did not wish to hide from the Lord in Christian love how I have considered his condition in Christian compassion, and have brought before the gracious mercy of the Most High what He might wish to give me to recognize concerning this matter.

2. Whereupon I report this to the Lord: that I have attained such contemplation <note>original: "Beschaulichkeit." A deep, meditative insight or spiritual vision.</note> within that same gracious mercy regarding the Lord’s condition and temptation, and have recognized the cause of it. I wish to briefly outline this for the Lord as a reminder, so that he may weigh it within himself.

3. The first cause of such a manifest temptation is the conflict between the supernatural, immeasurable love of GOD—the Divine good will—and the creaturely will of man. The human will does not want to entirely surrender itself and trust in such great grace of GOD, which is offered to it out of pure love; instead, it seeks its own selfhood <note>original: "Ichheit." A central Böhme term for the ego or the "I-complex" that asserts itself against God.</note> and the self-love of this transitory being, and loves itself and the essence of this world more than GOD.

4. Thus, a person is tempted by his own nature, which stands in its <term>Center</term> <note>original: "Centro." Böhme uses this to refer to the inner point or source from which a being’s life-force and qualities emerge.</note> outside the love of GOD, in sheer anguish, strife, and contrariety. Into this nature, the Devil shoots his false desire, in order to lead the person away from such high grace and love of GOD.

5. This temptation is the greatest, and it is precisely the struggle which Christ, with His infused love, maintains within human nature against such selfhood—as well as against GOD'S wrath, sin, death, the devil, and hell. Here, the human dragon <note>A symbolic representation of the fallen, selfish nature of man.</note> is meant to be swallowed up by the love of Christ and <term>transmuted</term> <note>original: "transmutiret." An alchemical term used here spiritually to describe the transformation of the soul’s base nature into something divine.</note> into an Angelic image <note>original: "Englisches Bild." In 17th-century German, "englisch" typically meant "angelic" (of the angels) rather than "English" (of England).</note>.

6. And if the love of GOD in Christ had not been poured into you, you would not have this struggle; rather, the dragon—as the false devil-will—would retain its natural right.

9. 10. 11. Böhme frequently warns that the ego tries to "own" spiritual gifts, which leads to spiritual pride.</note>, and to work within it in its own power. Understand the nature of the soul, which outside of GOD’s light is a dragon like Lucifer; it wants to possess the light as its own. But this dragon does not want to surrender its natural right; it wants to be a maker and creator of Divine power, and to live within it in great joy in its own fire-nature <term>Feuers-Natur: Böhme’s concept of the soul’s base essence—a consuming, hungry fire that must be transformed by the light of love to find peace.</term>, and that cannot be.

12. This dragon, as the fire-nature with its own will, must allow itself to be transformed into a love-fire and abandon its natural right: He, however, does not like to do this, but looks around during such a transformation

# Fifth Letter.
## To Mr. Christian Bernhard.
### From October 13, 1623.

### Summaries.

Wishes. §. 1. God opens His door of grace more and more, so that the hearts of many are touched, 2. and the new birth appears in great power even among the prominent people of the world. 3. A special example of this, 4. worked through the Author's little book on Repentance. 5. The Author reports this to encourage others. 6. Also, several Pharisees <note>Used here to describe legalistic or hypocritical religious authorities.</note> have been improved through his writings, and even high potentates have been moved, 7. besides the scholars, with whom he has had much conversation <note>original: "Conversation." In the 17th century, this meant social interaction and shared life, not just talking.</note>. 8. Yet the wolf also stands everywhere behind the lamb and wants to devour it. In the same place <note>original: "ibid."</note>. Therefore we should pray and be patient: all things must work for the best for God's children. 9. 10.

### Our salvation in the life of Jesus Christ in us!

Much beloved Sir, Brother Christian, I wish you God’s active power, that the wellspring in the life of Jesus Christ may well up abundantly in you, and your soul may be constantly refreshed in the same, and drink of this holy water, and also grow therein, flourish, and bear much good fruit, alongside your physical welfare! And I rejoice in your happy arrival, that God has helped you home again in good health.

2. You should also know that I, praise God, am still in good health and active in my talent <note>A reference to the biblical Parable of the Talents; Böhme views his writing and spiritual insight as a gift he must put to use for God.</note>: for God has opened His door of grace to me more and more, and not only to me, but also to many others who have received these writings to read, whose hearts God has touched, so that they have entered into repentance and conversion.

In this speaking, the Divine Sun of the kingdom of joy and great knowledge rose within him, and his heart and mind were completely turned around and renewed.

## Sixth Letter.
### To N. N. 1623.
### Summaries.

A wish. §. 1. What a true Christian is and why he is called a Christian? 2. 3. A Christian eats of the **Word of the Lord** <note>original Latin: "Verbo Domini"</note>, 4. Christ dwells in him, 5. through an **essential grace** <term>essentielle Gnade: Grace that is not just a legal decree, but a substantial spiritual presence that transforms the believer's inner nature</term>. 6. No outward imputation <note>The idea that God simply "counts" a person as righteous without changing their heart</note> suffices; 7. the person must turn back; 8. for what is born of the flesh is flesh. 9. Christ proclaims God's Word and will within ourselves, 10. so that lust is killed, 11. the temperament is restored through the **tincture** <term>Tinctur: In Böhme's terminology, a spiritual "dye" or life-force that can transmute the "lead" of the fallen soul into the "gold" of spiritual life</term> of the blood of Christ, 12. and the wrath is transformed into love. 13. 14. Therefore we must **put on Christ** <note>A biblical metaphor for taking on Christ's nature and identity</note>, 15. so that reconciliation may happen within us. 16. The true Adamic image in us dwells in Paradise. 17. Every Christian eats of his original state: 18. however, the spiritual mouth in man is also opened through Christ, 19. 20. who is the only sacrifice of reconciliation that must occur within us. 21. 22. Also, Christ is the action within us, 23. helps us carry the yoke of sin, 24. and overcome the wrath. 25. Therefore, a Christian must be a **cross-bearer**. 26. 27. Concerning [false] faith, nothing is taught. 28. 29. Christ alone is the Father's will; 30. 31. also, in Him alone is mercy. 32. He takes the **resigned** <term>gelassenen: From 'Gelassenheit', the mystical practice of yielding one's own will and ego completely to God</term> will into Himself, 33. and **tinctures** it into an angelic image. 34. That same angelic life hungers for the fiery soul, 35. and the soul sinks into the newborn will; 36. the new will, however, becomes **essential** in the soul. 37. This essence is called **Sophia** <term>Sophia: Divine Wisdom, often depicted by Böhme as a feminine spiritual principle or the "heavenly bride" of the soul</term>; and Christ and the person believe here on one ground. 38. What is true faith? 39. Namely, a spiritual eating. 40. Essential faith is a glimmering fire, 41. which is kindled by God's love. 42. Parable of the sun and the earth. 43. The ground of the soul is the field. 44. A Christian must place his hope in God alone. 45. His good fruits are good teaching and conduct. 46. The action must be present. 47.

# Sixth Letter

### Y 5

gives, when I perceive that our **paradisiacal Pearl-Tree** <term>Perlen-Baum: A central Böhmean metaphor for the growth of the divine life within the soul, representing the flourishing of the Holy Spirit and the "Pearl of Great Price."</term> grows green in my members and produces fruit, to our eternal delight.

3. And I wish herewith to indicate to the Lord <note>Here "Lord" refers to the recipient of the letter, a title of respect for a social peer or superior.</note> from my few gifts and knowledge, what a Christian is, and why he is called a Christian; namely, that he alone is a Christian who has become capable of this high title within himself; who, with the **inward ground** <term>inwendiger Grund: The deepest, most essential part of the soul where the human meets the divine</term>, the mind, and the will, has turned himself toward the gifted grace in Christ Jesus, and has become in his soul’s will like a young child that longs only for the mother's breasts, that has a thirst for the mother and sucks the mother's breasts, from which it lives.

4. So also, that man alone is a Christian whose soul and mind enter back into the first mother from which man's life sprouted (as into the **eternal Word** <note>original: "ewige Wort"</note>, which has revealed itself with the true milk of salvation in our humanity—which is otherwise blind to God), and who drinks this mother-milk into his hungry soul. From this, the new spiritual humanity takes its origin, and the fiery soul, through the Father’s property, attains the place of the **Love of God**—in which place the Father brings forth his beloved Son. In this place alone is found the **temple of the Holy Spirit** who dwells in us, and here alone is understood the spiritual mouth of the soul, which eats Christ’s flesh and drinks his blood.

5. For he alone is a Christian in whom Christ dwells, lives, and is; in whom Christ—according to the inward ground of the soul and the heavenly essence that faded in Adam—has risen and become alive. He is one who has put on Christ’s victory over God's wrath, and also over hell, devil, death, and sin (as Christ's humanity, suffering, death, and resurrection) in his inward ground. There, the **woman’s seed** <note>A reference to Genesis 3:15, interpreted as Christ within the believer</note> (as Christ in his overcoming) also overcomes within him, and daily crushes the head of the **serpent** <note>The "serpent" represents the selfish, fallen will of the flesh</note> in the evil will of the flesh, and kills the sinful lusts of the flesh.

6. For in Christ alone are we accepted into the **Divine Sonship** <note>original: "Göttliche Kindschaft"</note> and as heirs of Christ; not through

<summary>Böhme defines a "true Christian" not by outward profession, but as one who undergoes an internal rebirth, drinking from the "mother-milk" of the Eternal Word and allowing Christ to overcome the sinful nature within.</summary>

...an outward foreign appearance of a special acceptance of grace, through the foreign merit of an imputed grace from without; but through a childlike, indwelling, member-like, essential grace, where the conqueror of death—namely, Christ—with His life, essence, and power within us, rises from our death and rules and works in us, as a branch on its vine, as the scriptures of the apostles testify throughout.

7. He is no Christian who only comforts himself with the suffering, death, and satisfaction of Christ, and reckons the same to himself as a gift of grace, yet remains an **unregenerate wild beast**; such a "Christian" is every godless person. For everyone would gladly be saved through a gift of grace; even the devil would gladly become an angel again through a grace accepted from the outside.

8. But that he should turn back, and become like a child, and be born anew from God’s **grace-water of love** and the Holy Spirit—that does not suit his taste. Neither does it suit the **nominal Christian** <term>Titel-Christ: Literally a "Title-Christian"; one who carries the name of Christ but lacks the internal spiritual reality.</term>, who indeed wraps the **cloak of grace** <note>original: "Gnaden-Mantel." This refers to the theological concept of "imputed righteousness," where Christ's merit covers the sinner. Böhme warns that this "cloak" is useless if the person underneath it has not been internally transformed.</note> of Christ around himself, but does not wish to enter into childhood and the new birth. Yet Christ says that otherwise he cannot see the kingdom of God.

9. For what is born of the flesh is flesh (**John 3:6**) and cannot inherit God's kingdom; to be **carnally minded** <term>fleischlich gesinnet: Thinking and acting according to worldly, selfish, or physical impulses rather than divine inspiration.</term> is enmity against God, but to be spiritually minded is life and peace. And only he who is born of God hears God’s word. For the Spirit of grace in Christ alone hears God’s word.

10. For no one has ever seen God, except the Son, who is in the Father’s immeasurable bosom; He proclaims to us God’s word and will within our very selves (**John 1:18**), so that we hear and understand His will and benevolence within us and desire to follow it. Yet we are often held back by the outward sinful flesh, so that the effect of this same Divine power does not always manifest in the **outward form** <note>original: "äusserliche Figur."</note>; it does, however, manifest in the inward form in the inner spiritual world, of which St. Paul says: **Our citizenship is in heaven** <note>original: "Unser Wandel ist im Himmel" (Philippians 3:20). The word "Wandel" implies one's entire way of life, conduct, and dwelling place.</note>.

### Sixth Letter.

11. This is also why all God’s holy ones, and especially Saint Paul, have lamented that although they possess an earnest will and serve God with the disposition of the **inner ground**, they nonetheless serve the law of sin with the flesh, so that the flesh lusts against the spirit. **Romans 7:25**. <note>original: "mit dem Gemüthe des inwendigen Grundes." Böhme uses "Gemüthe" to describe the seat of the will and emotions, and "inner ground" to describe the deepest, divine center of the human soul.</note> This lust is daily drowned and killed in the death of Christ through the inner ground; but this occurs only in those in whom Christ has risen from the dead. In such people, there remains nothing worthy of condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus. For the animal body belongs to the earth, but the spiritual body belongs to God. However, whoever does not possess this spiritual body is "living dead" and neither hears nor perceives anything of the Spirit of God; for it is foolishness to him, according to the Scripture. **1 Corinthians 2:14**.

12. Therefore, all that is spoken solely of a grace and forgiveness of sins received from the outside is not sufficiently understood or explained. The forgiveness of sins and the adoption into grace consists in the justification through the blood and death of Christ; here, Christ's heavenly blood **tinctured** us. <note>original: "tingirte." An alchemical term used by Böhme to describe how Christ’s divine nature permeates and transforms the "base metal" of the human soul into "spiritual gold."</note> It overcame the wrath of God in our souls and in the internal divine ground of the Being of Eternity with the highest love of the Deity, in the name of Jesus. It **transmuted** us back into divine humility and obedience, so that the torn **temperament** of our human property—once characterized by obedience and goodwill—entered back into the equality or union of properties. <term>Temperatur: In Böhme's thought, this refers to the perfect balance or "harmony" of the spiritual forces within a person. Sin "tore" this balance, and Christ restores it.</term>

13. There, the Father’s wrath (which had been awakened in our life-properties and had made itself the ruler in soul and body, whereby we were dead to the kingdom of heaven and had become children of wrath) was changed back into the Single Love and equality of God. Our human <term>Eigen-Wille</term> <note>Self-will; the rebellious desire to be independent of God.</note> died away in the death of Christ to its <term>Ichheit</term> <note>Selfhood or "I-ness"; the ego-driven state of being.</note> and its own-willing, and the first human will—which God breathed from His Spirit into Adam—blossomed forth again through the overcoming sweetness of God in Christ’s heavenly blood. There, the devil and hell, who held man captive, were put to mockery. For that was the withered rod of Aaron, which

<summary>Böhme explains that true salvation is an internal transmutation where Christ's "heavenly blood" restores the soul's harmony and kills the selfish "I-ness" of the fallen human will. He emphasizes that mere external belief is insufficient compared to this profound inner rebirth.</summary>
<keywords>inner ground, justification, tincture, self-will, selfhood, Aaron's rod, spiritual body, divine humility, transmutation, temperament</keywords>

### Sixth Letter.

...bloomed in a single night and bore sweet almonds, signifying this. **Numbers 17:8; Hebrews 9:4.**

14. Now, just as sin came from one, and pressed from One upon All; so also the sweet grace and overcoming in Christ pressed from One upon all; **Romans 5:18**. In the single Adamic soul, death and wrath were shattered in Christ, and a possibility for grace was opened through this shattering of death: through which shattered gate the soulish <term>will</term><note>The "soulish will" (seelische Wille) refers to the human capacity for choice and desire that originates in the soul's core.</note> may turn itself back into the first Mother, from whence it came in the beginning, as into the childhood or new birth of a new life and willing. There it may reach the sweet blood of Jesus Christ—which shattered the gates of death in our humanity in Christ, and changed the wrath of God in our humanity into love within Himself—therein the poor captive soul drinks from God's fountain and refreshes itself in its <term>fire-breath</term><note>original: "Feuer-Odem." In Böhme's cosmology, the soul is a "fire-spirit" that needs the "water" of divine love to become a light; without it, the fire remains a dark hunger or wrath.</note>, from which the new greening grows forth, as the soul's hunger and desire becomes substantial and essential in the blood of Christ, according to the heavenly manner.

15. Now, just as the shattering of death had to occur in Christ’s person in our soul and humanity—so that eternity in Christ (with which He had come from heaven, and was also simultaneously in heaven, **John 3:13**) overcame time, as the life and will of time, and changed time with its will into the eternal will of the Godhead, and such had to happen in our assumed humanity; so also, in the same way, our soul’s desire must take that same eternal will in Christ—where time and eternity stand in likeness—into itself, and through that same power sink itself back into childhood, as into grace, so that the same inner Paradisiacal ground, which died in Adam, might <term>green forth</term><note>original: "ausgrüne." Böhme frequently uses the imagery of plants and "greening" (viriditas) to describe the organic, living growth of the spirit within the soul.</note> again in the will of Christ’s obedience, through His heavenly and human blood, which He assumed from us.

16. In ourselves, the reconciliation must become manifest through Christ’s once-and-for-all reconciliation; truly through that which happened once in Christ’s blood and death; but that same "once-happened" event in Christ must also do its work in me; it must now, through the shedding of Christ’s blood, also in me

### Sixth Letter. 333

...occurred. Christ also pours His heavenly blood into the desire of my faith within my poor soul, and <term>tinctures</term><note>original: "tingiret." An alchemical term used by Böhme to describe the spiritual process where one substance transforms the quality of another—specifically, how divine love transforms the "fire" of God's wrath.</note> the wrath of God within it, so that the first <term>Adamic image</term><note>The original, perfect state of humanity created in God's likeness before the Fall.</note> of God might be seen again, and become seeing, hearing, feeling, tasting, and smelling.

17. For that same image of the heavenly <term>world-essence</term><note>The spiritual substance or "being" of the divine realm.</note> which died in Adam, being the true paradisical one, does not then dwell in the four elements; its essence and life do not consist in this world, but in heaven—which is revealed within us in Christ, as in a pure <term>Holy Element</term><note>original: "H. Element." In Böhme's cosmology, this is the "Fifth Element" or quintessence: the spiritual substance from which the four physical elements (earth, air, fire, water) originated.</note> from which the four elements sprouted at the beginning of time. And this same inner, new spiritual person eats Christ’s flesh and drinks His blood, for he lives and is in Christ: Christ is his trunk, and he is a branch on the trunk.

18. For every spirit eats from that which is its <term>original state</term><note>original: "Urstand." The fundamental source or ground from which a thing's existence arises.</note>: just as the animalistic, mortal soul eats from the <term>Spirit of the World</term><note>original: "Spiritu Mundi." The governing spirit of the physical universe, including the influence of the stars and the four physical elements.</note>, from the stars and the four elements, from the kingdom of this world. But the true, eternal soul, which was breathed into man from the eternal Word as a divine life—this soul eats from its Mother, that is, from the holy, substantial Word of God.

19. Because this was not possible for the soul in its exiled quality after its separation from God, the same Word of Life came out again, like its true mother, to the exiled soul here in this <term>vale of misery</term><note>original: "Jammerthal." A common historical and biblical expression for the earthly world of suffering and trial.</note>, into the prison of hell, and brought its heavenly essence into our human essence as a <term>body</term><note>original: "Corpus."</note> for the soul. It surrounded our poor, captive soul with it, and through the <term>tincture of love</term><note>original: "Liebe Tinktur." The healing power of divine love that "colors" and transforms the soul's nature.</note> it sprinkled open its dead heavenly mouth within the wrath of God, so that the poor soul might again eat heavenly manna. This eating stood again in the <term>trial</term><note>original: "Proba." A test or proving ground.</note> within Christ's person—with our assumed humanity—during Christ’s temptation in the wilderness, where Adam in Christ again ate manna from Paradise for forty days.

20. Therefore I say: if someone is a Christian, he is not one through an outward appearance of grace attributed to him from the outside; sin is not forgiven him through a one-time outward speaking of words, like a lord in this

### Sixth Letter. 334

...[as if] the world grants a murderer his life through an external, imputed grace: No, that does not hold before God.

21. There is no grace by which we can attain the status of <term>childship</term><note>original: "Kind-schaft." Often translated as "sonship," this refers to the spiritual state of being a child of God, restored to the divine family.</note> except purely in the blood and death of Christ. God alone has set Him forth as a <term>Throne of Grace</term><note>original: "Gnaden-Throne." A reference to the Mercy Seat or *Kapporet* of the Ark of the Covenant, where God’s presence met humanity; Böhme identifies this entirely with Christ.</note>, in His own love, which He introduced into Him in the sweet name of **Jesus** out of **Jehovah** <note>Böhme frequently uses a mystical etymology where the name "Jesus" is the "sweetening" or "love-filling" of the stern, fiery name of "Jehovah" (the Father's wrath).</note>. He is the only sacrifice that God accepts, which can reconcile His wrath.

22. But if this same sacrifice is to benefit me, it must happen **within me**. The Father must beget or instill His Son into the desire of my faith, so that my hunger for faith grasps Him; and if my soul's hunger for faith grasps Him, as in His promised Word, then I put Him on in the entire process of <term>justification</term><note>original: "Rechts-fertigung." While a standard theological term, Böhme views justification not as a legal decree, but as an actual internal transformation.</note> within my internal <term>ground</term><note>original: "Grund." The deepest, most fundamental center of the human soul.</note>, and immediately the slaying of wrath, the devil, death, and hell proceeds from Christ’s death within me.

23. For I can do nothing, I am dead to myself; but Christ in me does it: when He rises within me, I am dead to myself according to the true man, and He is my life; and what I then live, I live for Him, and not for **mine-ness** <note>original: "Meinheit." Böhme's term for self-interest or the proprietary sense of "mine."</note>, for grace kills my will and establishes itself as Lord in place of my **I-hood** <note>original: "Jchheit." The ego or self-centered will that must be surrendered to God.</note>, so that I may be a work of God, who does with it what He wills.

24. And I live then in two kingdoms: as with the external mortal man in the vanity of time, wherein the **yoke of sin** still lives; this Christ takes upon Himself in the inner kingdom of the Divine World, and helps my soul to carry it.

25. For the yoke of this world is Christ's burden, which He is to carry until He delivers the kingdom, which was given to Him, back to His Father, as He said: *All power is given unto me in heaven and on earth by my Father*; Thus, this burden is also given to Him: that He should carry God's wrath, hell, death, and all evil within us, as <term>Isaiah</term><note>original: "Esajas." Refers to Isaiah 53:4.</note> says: *He took upon Himself our sickness, and loaded upon Himself our pains; but we considered Him to be the one who was thus struck down, punished, and martyred by God.*

<meta>catchword: 26.</meta>

<summary>Böhme explains that salvation is not a mere legal pardon but an internal process where Christ is born within the soul, replacing the human ego ("I-hood") with divine will. He describes the believer as living simultaneously in two realms: the temporal world of sin and the internal kingdom where Christ carries the soul's burdens.</summary>

### Sixth Letter.

<page-num>335</page-num>

26. Therefore, a Christian must be a <term>Cross-bearer</term><note>original: "Creutz-Träger." For Böhme, being a Christian is not a passive state but an active participation in the suffering and "cross" of Christ as the soul struggles against its own selfish nature.</note>. For as soon as Christ is born in him, the storm of hell and the <term>wrath of God</term><note>original: "Zornes GOttes." Böhme views "wrath" as a literal spiritual force within "eternal nature" that must be transmuted into love.</note> in eternal nature begins; then hell is disturbed within the person, and the serpent is trampled. From this comes the great unrest, persecution, and disgrace from the devil and the corrupted world that falls upon the outer, sinful man. There, the outer sinful man must allow himself to be judged by God's strict justice in wrath—to be condemned by the "children of wrath"—because another person lives within him who is not like the outer, mortal one. Thus, God's justice in wrath carries out its judgment over the "house of sin," as do all the servants of God's wrath.

27. In that place, Christ helps to bear the yoke, and the person is offered up to the justice of God in wrath through <term>Christ's process</term><note>original: "Christi Prozeß." This refers to the lived sequence of Christ's life: his birth, suffering, death, and resurrection, which Böhme believes every believer must re-enact internally.</note>, through contempt and mockery, and through his suffering and death; thus, he becomes like the image of Christ.

28. The Holy Scripture testifies in all places that we are justified from sin through faith in Christ—not through the works of our own merits, but through the blood and death of Christ. This is indeed taught by many, but understood correctly by very few of those who teach it.

29. We are certainly taught about <term>imputed grace</term><note>original: "zugerechnete Gnade." A common Reformation doctrine that Christ's righteousness is "credited" to the believer's account. Böhme warns that this can become a hollow concept if no inner change occurs.</note>; but as to what faith is, how it is born, what its essence and being are, and how it takes hold of the merit of Christ along with grace—on these points, the majority of people are mute and blind. They remain stuck in a <term>historical faith</term><note>original: "Historischen Glauben." Böhme’s term for merely believing that the stories of the Bible are true facts without having a personal, living experience of the Spirit.</note> (James 2:17), which is only a form of knowledge. With this, a person merely tickles and comforts himself amidst sin and death, flattering himself through such imagination and calling himself a "Christian." Yet, he has not yet become capable or worthy of this high title and is only a <term>Title-Christian</term><note>original: "Titel-Christ." One who holds the name of Christ as a label or honorific without the underlying spiritual reality.</note>, covered from the outside with Christ’s purple cloak. Of such people, the prophet says: *With their lips they draw near to me, but their heart is far from me* (Isaiah 29:13, Mark 7:6). And Christ says: *Not everyone who says to me, "Lord, Lord," shall enter the kingdom of heaven, but he who does the will of my Father in heaven* (Matthew 7:21).

<meta>catchword: 30.</meta>

<summary>Böhme argues that true Christianity requires an internal "cross-bearing" where the believer’s old nature is judged and replaced by the image of Christ, contrasting this with a "historical faith" that relies on labels rather than inner transformation.</summary>

30. Now Christ alone is the will of the Father, within which lies the acceptance of grace and the status of children; and no one can perform the Father's will of love, except for the one and only <term>Throne of Grace</term><note>original: "Gnaden-Thron." A biblical reference to the Mercy Seat, here representing Christ as the place where God's judgment meets His mercy.</note>, Christ Himself, as the Scripture says: no one can call God a Lord without the Holy Spirit within them.

31. For we do not know how to pray before God as is fitting, but He, the Holy Spirit in Christ, intercedes for us ourselves with unspeakable sighs before God within our own being, as it pleases God, Romans 8:26. We can neither do nor achieve anything through our own willing or knowing; He is hidden too deeply from us. For it does not depend on anyone's knowing, willing, running, or racing, but on God's mercy. Romans 9:16.

32. Now there is no mercy except in Christ alone: if I am to reach mercy, I must reach Christ within me; if my sin is to be wiped out within me, Christ must do it with His blood and death and with His victory within me. If I am to believe, then the Spirit, the desire, and the will of Christ must believe within my desire and will, for I cannot believe on my own.

33. He, however, takes my will which is surrendered to Him, and enfolds it into His own will, and leads it through His victory into God. There He represents the will of my soul within His own will before God, and I am accepted as a child of grace in His will of love.

34. For the Father has revealed His love in Christ, and Christ reveals that same love in my surrendered will; Christ draws my will into Himself, and clothes it with His blood and death, and <term>tinctures</term><note>original: "tingiret." Böhme uses alchemical language here; a "tincture" is a spiritual force that penetrates and transforms a substance from within.</note> it with the highest <term>tincture</term> of Divine power; there it is <term>transmuted</term><note>original: "transmutiret." To transform or change the very nature of a thing, like base metal into gold.</note> into an angelic image, and receives a Divine life.

35. Now that same life begins to hunger after its <term>body</term><note>original: "Corpus."</note>, which body is the corrupted, <term>fiery soul</term><note>original: "feurische Seele." In Böhme's system, the soul is naturally a dark fire of desire that must be "tinctured" by the light of Christ to find peace.</note> from which the will entered into Christ. Thus the new life in Christ now also tinctures the soul, so that the soul receives a true Divine hunger in this spirit of the will, and becomes desirous of Divine grace; and

->Sixth Letter. 337<-

begins in this Divine Will-Spirit in Christ to examine itself: seeing what it is, how in its own properties it had been separated from God, and how it lay imprisoned in God’s wrath. It recognizes its own abominations, as well as its deformity before God’s angels, finding that it has nothing with which it might shield itself. For it sees that it stands in the jaws of death and hell, surrounded by evil spirits who constantly introduce their desires into it to destroy it.

36. Then it sinks into that same newborn Will-Spirit and immerses itself in the purest humility; thus the Spirit of Christ seizes it and leads it into this new Will-Spirit, so that the soul feels it <term>essentially</term><note>original: "essentialiter." In Böhme's thought, this means the soul experiences God as a tangible, living reality rather than an abstract idea.</note>: there, the Divine vision of joy rises within the soul like a new eye, in which the fiery soul receives the <term>Entity and Essence</term><note>original: "Ens und Wesen." "Ens" is a philosophical term for the fundamental "stuff" or spiritual substance of a thing.</note> of the Divine Light, for which it hungers and thirsts according to God’s grace, and enters into powerful <term>penitence</term><note>original: "Pönitenz."</note> or repentance, and regrets the evil it has committed.

37. And in this hunger and thirst, it receives Christ’s flesh and blood. For the new Will-Spirit—which initially entered into the grace of Christ and which Christ has taken into Himself—now becomes <term>substantial</term><note>original: "substantia-lisch."</note> or essential through the soul’s <term>magnetic compression</term><note>original: "magnetisch Einpressen." Böhme uses the metaphor of a magnet to describe how intense spiritual desire "pulls" or "compacts" divine spirit into a tangible internal reality.</note>, hunger, and desire.

38. And this essence is called ***Sophia***, as the essential Wisdom or the Body of Christ; and in this, faith stands in the Holy Spirit; here Christ and the soul believe in one single ground.

39. For true faith is not a thought or a mere acceptance of history—where a person merely forces themselves to believe that Christ died for their sins—but it is a taking of the promised grace of Christ. The soul takes Christ into itself; it <term>compresses</term><note>original: "impresset."</note> Him into its hunger with His heavenly flesh and blood, and with the grace which God offers in Christ.

40. Christ feeds the soul with the essence of ***Sophia***, as with His body and blood, just as He then said: *Unless you eat the flesh of the Son of Man, you have no life in Him; but whoever eats the same remains in Christ and Christ in him.* John 6:53. <note>The author provides a translation of the Latin Vulgate/Gospel context into the vernacular.</note>

->### Sixth Letter.<-
->44.<-

41. And herein also consist <note>original: "Christi Testamenta"</note> **Christ's Testaments** and the true Christian faith: For an unsubstantial faith is like a smoldering fire or mold in a damp place that would like to burn but has no proper <term>Ens</term><note>A Latin term Böhme uses to mean "essence" or the fundamental spiritual "stuff" that gives a thing its reality.</note> for it. But when a proper <term>Ens</term> is given to it, that tiny little spark of fire increases, from which a beautiful light arises that shines all around. Then it becomes manifest how such a fire and beautiful light lay hidden within the wood, which was not recognized before.

42. This is also how it is to be understood in a child of GOD: because the poor soul is wrapped in the <note>original: "Grimme GOTTES"</note> **Wrath of GOD**, it is like a smoldering little wick that would like to burn, but cannot because of the vanity of sins and the anger of GOD. But when the soul, as that tiny spark of Divine fire, receives into itself Christ’s **Love-Essence**—meaning Christ’s flesh and blood—then that little spark begins to become a great fire and light, which shines and gleams all around with beautiful virtues and good works, and lives in great patience amidst the vanity of this world, yet grows forth like a beautiful flower out of the wild earth.

43. We have a parable of this in the sun and the earth: if the sun did not shine upon the earth, no fruit would grow. But when the sun shines upon the earth and penetrates into the earth's <term>Ens</term>, then the earth’s essence catches the sun's power within itself, from which a great hunger arises in the earth’s <term>Ente</term><note>A variation of "Ens," referring to the internal substance or "being-ness" of the earth.</note> for the sun's power. And this same hunger compresses the sun's power, and out of that hunger of the earth’s <term>Entis</term><note>The genitive form of Ens, meaning "of the essence."</note>, which reaches upward for the sun's essence, a plant is drawn out of the earth with a stalk, in which the sun's <term>Ens</term> and power go upward within the growth. Thus the sun, with its rays of light, becomes substantial within the essence of the earth in the stalk and the root. And one sees how, through the power of the sun and the constellations in the <term>Spirit of the World</term><note>original: "Spiritu Mundi." In Böhme's view, this is the "soul of the world," the underlying physical-spiritual force that governs nature.</note>, another body is formed out of the stalk, different from the root in the earth; how the stalk leads into a bud toward a beautiful blossom and afterward toward the fruit. One also sees how the sun afterward ripens that same fruit from time to time and makes it entirely lovely.

<summary>Böhme explains that true faith requires a spiritual "substance" (Ens) to shine, comparing the soul's growth through Christ's love to a plant rising from the dark earth toward the sun.</summary>

44. This is also how it is to be understood regarding man: The ground of the soul is the **Divine Field**; when it receives the **Divine Sunshine** into itself, a **Divine Growth** springs forth from it. This is the **New Birth** <note>original: "Wieder-Geburt"</note> of which Christ speaks in John 3:7. This growth must now be nourished and raised from above, by the Divine Sun and by the **Divine Constellation** <note>original: "Göttliche Gestirne"</note>—acting as the Divine Power—until it becomes a **Divine Corpus** <term>Corpus</term><note>Latin for "body." Böhme uses this to describe the substantial, spiritual form that the soul takes on through regeneration, contrasting it with the physical body.</note> of a Divine and **angelic** <note>original: "englischen." In Böhme's 17th-century German, this almost always refers to the nature of angels, not the English nation.</note> figure, just like the grain that forms upon the stalk.

45. And just as the grain upon the stalk must endure in rain, wind, and tempest, in heat and cold, and allow the sun to ripen it: so must a **Christian** grow amidst thorns in this world. He must stand within the awakened **Wrath of GOD**, in the kingdom of the Devil, among many godless people, and let himself be struck with mockery and contempt; yet he must direct his hope solely and alone, away from all creatures, toward the **Divine Sun**, and let himself be ripened by it and born into a heavenly fruit.

46. Neither houses of stone nor **human statutes** <note>original: "Menschen-Satzungen," referring to ecclesiastical laws or man-made religious rules.</note> give birth to him; rather, it is the Divine Sun within the Divine Constellation of the powers of the **Word of GOD** in the temple of **Jesus Christ**, so that he is a **branch on the vine of Christ** and brings forth good grapes, which the Divine Sun ripens. These grapes are eaten by God's children as His dear members, through which they also grow green in and with Him; such grapes are good teaching, life, and deeds.

47. It must come to **action and fruit-bearing** within a person; otherwise, the new birth is not yet manifest in him, and the noble branch is not yet born. No amount of self-satisfaction <note>original: "Kizeln," literally "tickling," implying a superficial or sensory religious pleasure.</note>, comforting, nor boasting of a faith helps, if that faith does not become a **God-like child** in essence and will, which bears Divine fruits.

48. All of this, over which people now strive and fight—even ruining land and people—is but an **empty husk** without fruit, and belongs to the fiery world <note>Böhme refers to the "firing" or "burning" world of judgment and temporal vanity.</note> for separation. There is no true understanding in any **party** <term>Parthey</term><note>Referring to the warring religious and political factions of the Thirty Years' War era.</note>; they all fight only over the Name and Will of GOD, and no party wishes to actually *do* it; they intend nothing but their own honor—

...and lust of the flesh: If they were Christians, they would have no strife.

49. A good tree bears good fruit for everyone; and even though it must suffer when the wind often strikes off its branches and fruit, and the sun withers them, and even when they have become ripe, the sows eat them or they are trampled underfoot, it still works constantly toward other good fruit.

50. In the same way, a true Christian in Christ can will nothing other than what Christ himself wills within him; although he must suffer when his good fruits—which green and grow from the inward man—are often trampled and corrupted by his evil flesh and blood, as well as by the devil’s wind and the world's malice, yet the tree of the new growth remains standing in the life of Christ. It greens forth through the outward, mortal man without any stopping, just as eternity greens through time and gives life and power to time. And just as the day greens forth through the night and transforms the night into day—where the night still remains in itself but is not recognized within the day—so also the Divine Day greens forth through our eternal night within us. It transforms the night, as **GOD'S** wrath, hell, death, anguish, and eternal perdition, into the Divine **Kingdom of Joy** <note>original: "Freudenreich"</note>, even though the dark night with the serpent’s <term>Essence</term> <note>original: "Ens." A Latin term Böhme uses to describe the fundamental "being" or spiritual substance of a thing.</note> and poison rages and strives against it in flesh and blood.

51. Therefore, beloved sir and Christian brother, we must strive more after the growth of the noble <term>Pearl-Tree</term> <note>A signature Böhme metaphor for the soul's inner spiritual development and the blossoming of heavenly wisdom.</note>, and how we may come to such a thing, rather than running after useless chatter and trifles, where one brother despises, slanders, condemns as a heretic, and gives to the devil another brother for the sake of an opinion he has made for himself.

52. I tell you, in my **Insight** <note>original: "Erkenntniß"</note> given to me by **GOD**, that it is nothing but the deceit of the devil, who leads us poor humans along in opinions, contempt, and mockery, so that we bicker over the remedy and meanwhile lose love and faith and do not come to the **New Birth** <note>original: "neue Geburt"</note>.

# Sixth Letter.

53. Our entire religion is merely a child’s path <note>Böhme emphasizes that true spirituality is found in simplicity and humility, like a child, rather than in complex intellectual debates.</note>: that we should completely depart from our own knowing, willing, running, and disputing, and resolve to step onto the path that leads us back into our lost fatherland—how we may come again to our Mother, who bore us out of herself in the beginning.

54. If we now wish to do this, we must not come to her willfully, in pomp and contempt of her children (our fellow Christians or members). For we are the Prodigal Son who became a swineherd, and we have shamefully squandered our paternal inheritance with the devil’s and the world’s husks and swine. We must enter back into ourselves and properly consider ourselves and our Father’s house. We must take up the mirror of the Law and the Gospel before us and see how far we have stepped away from God’s righteousness and truth, as well as from brotherly love, and examine our hearts to see what they are inclined toward.

55. When we do this, we will find many hundreds of evil beasts within ourselves, which we have set up in God’s place and honor as God. We will then first see what kind of abominable beasts were revealed in Adam through false lust, and why God said to Adam: "The woman’s seed shall crush the head of the serpent" <note>A reference to Genesis 3:15, traditionally interpreted as the promise of a Savior who would defeat evil.</note>, as the head of these monstrous beasts.

56. For instance, we will first see in our desire the proud Lucifer, who has departed from Divine and brotherly humility, and who despises the members of his own body <note>Böhme refers to the "body of Christ," where fellow believers are "members" or parts of one another.</note>, setting himself above them as a god and lord in whom there is no Divine love—neither to love God nor his brothers.

57. Secondly, we will find a beast in our own nature <note>original: "Eigenschaft"</note> that is like a greedy sow, which pulls everything to itself and wants to eat and possess alone, desiring more than it needs so that the proud Lucifer can boast and show himself off as a "god over beings" <note>original: "Gott über Wesen." Böhme critiques the desire to dominate the very substance of life.</note> who can rule and has power and authority over his fellow-branches <note>original: "Mitäste." Böhme envisions humanity as branches on a single tree of life; to dominate others is to attack one's own tree.</note>. And we will see how this proud Lucifer has broken himself off from the Tree of Life and from the growth of love, wanting to be a tree of his own—which is why he then withered away from God.

# Sixth Letter.

58. Thirdly, we will find the poisonous, envious serpent in our nature, which stings all around it like a venom; this is **envy**, which grants no one as much as it grants itself. It stings and rides into other people's hearts, slandering them with words, and praises only the proud Lucifer <note>In Böhme’s thought, Lucifer is the archetype of the "Self-Will" that turned away from God's light to dwell in his own dark fire.</note> within itself, calling its own falsehood an "Angel of God."

59. Fourthly, we will find the fiery dragon sitting in hellish fire within our nature; this is **wrath**. When it cannot obtain what greed and envy desire, it wishes to strike with fists and take by force. It is so maddened that it bursts its own life with malice and shatters in fiery wickedness; it is entirely a dry branch on the tree, fit only for the fire.

60. Fifthly, we will find many hundreds of beasts in our desire, which **pride** <note>original: "Hoffart"</note> loves and honors before God, and which **greed** draws to itself as a treasure. Pride struts with these as if they were gods, and thus draws the life away from its brother, so that he must consume his life in misery and tribulation through such coercion.

61. Now, when a person gazes at himself in this mirror of his **selfhood** <term>Selbheit: Böhme’s term for the ego or the self-centered will that acts independently of God’s will</term>, and becomes aware of these evil beasts, he may well imagine them within himself. He should consider the heavy fall of Adam through this, and think that all these desires arose together from the monster of the serpent, through the Devil’s introduction of them into our first parents.

62. For all the properties of the desires lay in Adam in **equality** <note>Böhme believes that before the Fall, all human impulses were in a state of perfect "Temperament" or balance; no single emotion or desire dominated the others.</note>, and each loved the other. But through the Devil's envy—which awakened the false lust in Adam and Eva to test "inequality," to taste what is Evil and Good, to feel heat and cold, and to experience the multiplicity of properties—such false desires have arisen in man. Now, these desires attract and crave their own kind; each desire of these properties is a particular "hunger for life" in man which has broken away from the equality. It lusts against the love and equality of its fellow-branches or brothers, seeking to draw their life and nourishment to itself, to make itself lord over them, and to exist as a self-centered entity.

63. All of this is against the Divine Will and Ground, and is a perjury against God; it also runs against the course of nature, as one sees in the earth, the trees, and all plants—how everything stands and grows lovely together, and rejoices in One Mother, and how one branch on a tree infuses its sap and power into another, and each serves the other.

64. For human life was also like this (John 1), introduced from the eternal Word into the human image from the <term>clay of the earth</term> <note>original Latin: "Limo." In Böhme's thought, this "limus" or mud is the "quintessence" or spiritual extraction of the earth from which Adam was formed.</note> into a lovely equality, so that all the qualities of life stood in equal weight, in a <term>tempered balance</term> <note>original: "Temperatur." This refers to a state where no single quality or "element" dominates another, resulting in perfect harmony.</note> of one love, and loved themselves.

65. But when the Devil threw his poison and false desires into it, the qualities of life were torn apart into many desires; from this arose strife, sickness, shattering, and the coarseness of the body. Through the false desire and the introduction of animalistic qualities, the Image of God faded from the heavenly world-essence. Concerning this, God said to them: "On the day that you eat from the plant of the knowledge of Good and Evil, you shall die the death"—that is, you shall die to the Kingdom of God—which is exactly what happened.

66. And we should quite clearly imagine that this animalistic and false desire in man is the Serpent's Monster, and an enmity against God and the Kingdom of Heaven. In this state, we are nothing other than children of hell and the wrath of God, and we cannot inherit or possess the Kingdom of God in it. Furthermore, God is not manifest in any such desire, but only His wrath and the quality of the dark and earthly world. Within it, we live only for the vanity of this world and stand thereby upon the abyss of the dark world of God’s wrath—that is, upon hell, which every hour opens its jaws for these qualities and regards these qualities as its fruit and children, which it shall harvest and which belong to it by natural right. For these desires all arose from it, and they stand with their roots in the ground of hell and corruption, and not otherwise at all.

## Seventh Letter.
### To N. N. of Lübeck. <note>The initials "N. N." (Latin: *nomen nescio*) indicate that the recipient's name was withheld or unknown to the original editor.</note>
->From the 20th of April, 1624.<-

### Summaries.

Wishes. § 1. **God** leads those who love to Love. § 1–3. Reason and searching do not attain the true ground of Divine knowledge. 4. Searching must begin from within, in the hunger of the soul, not in the reason (ibid.) <note>original: "ibid.," abbreviation for the Latin *ibidem*, meaning "in the same place" or "as previously stated."</note>, and the soul must surrender all its power and will entirely to Love; 5. then the Spirit of **God** searches through it. 6. It is a very simple way of children to the highest wisdom, which the world does not know. 7. In the author's writings, one sees only the brilliance of the Divine mysteries; but where **God's** light itself catches fire in the soul, only then is the true <term>Theosophical</term> <note>Theosophical here refers to "Divine Wisdom" (from the Greek *theos* and *sophia*), a direct experiential knowledge of God rather than academic study.</note> Pentecostal school opened. 8. ## Our Salvation in the active Love of Jesus Christ within us!

My very dear and Christian Lord; <note>Böhme uses the formal "Herr" (Lord/Sir) to address his correspondent, a common polite address of the time.</note> I wish you high peace alongside heartfelt, brotherly love, and a shared longing that the true sun of the active love of **Jesus Christ** may constantly rise and shine in your soul, spirit, and body.

2. I received your letter dated January 24th <note>original: "unterm dato 24. Januarii," Latin for "under the date of Jan 24."</note> fourteen days after Easter, and I rejoiced to see therein that you are a hungry, zealous, and eager seeker and lover of the true Ground; for which, as I understand, you have diligently striven and searched.

3. That my writings have also come into your hands and that you find pleasure in them is certainly the cause and a Divine ordinance which leads those who love toward Love. God often uses foreign means to fulfill the loving desire, feeding it with His gift, and introducing an <term>Ens</term> <note>From the Latin for "being" or "essence." The searching must begin from within, in the hunger of the soul; for the searching of reason reaches only into its <term>Astrum</term> <note>Latin for "star" or "constellation." But the soul searches in its own *Astrum*, which is the inner spiritual world from which the visible world arose or flowed out, and in which the soul stands with its own Ground.

5. But if the soul wishes to search its own *Astrum* as the <term>Mysterium Magnum</term>, <note>Latin for "Great Mystery." It must first become like a child and turn toward its <term>Centro</term> <note>Latin for "Center." This is the point of divine origin or the "heart" within the soul where God dwells.</note> through great repentance, and wish to do nothing except what the Spirit of **God** wishes to search through it. # Eighth Letter.
## To Mr. N. N. <note>original: "N. N." This is a Latin abbreviation for *Nomen Nescio*, indicating the recipient's name was unknown or omitted by the original editor.</note>
### From April 25, 1624.
## Summaries.

In the tree of Christ we are all only One, which is Christ in us. §. 1-5. The world speaks of Christ out of habit. 6. The Son of God alone gives us the true science <note>original: "Wissenschaft." # Our salvation in the working love of Jesus Christ in us!

My beloved brother in the life of Jesus Christ, along with a heartfelt wish for God’s active love, that your noble little lily-twig <note>The "lily" is Böhme’s symbol for the spiritual rebirth and the coming era of peace and purity.</note>, which has sprouted in Christ, may grow large in God’s paradise in the power of Christ and bear much fruit, to the eternal joy of us all and our heavenly brotherhood!

2. I rejoice in my soul when I hear that a powerful, beautiful little branch has sprouted on our Tree of Life, Christ, and I hope to enjoy its good fruits as well.

3. Just as one branch on a tree enjoys the sap and power of another, and all grow and bear fruit in one power; so also are we all only One in the tree of Christ, which is Christ in us all.

4. Because you then freely and publicly confess this Tree of Life with mouth and heart, and conversely renounce the poison and error of Satan, I now wish for nothing more than that I might be able, in the power of this tree, which is Christ, to infuse you with the power I have received from Him, so that we, as members, may grow in one power.

5. And do not doubt me in this, that the Most High has born His lily-branch <term>lily-branch</term> <note>original: "Lilien-Zweig." In Böhme's mystical language, the lily represents the blossoming of the "New Man" or the spiritual rebirth within the soul.</note> within you; for without Divine power we have no desire nor hunger for God, and we also cannot recognize Him without His Spirit in us. Everything fundamental we know of Him comes from His revelation and working.

6. For although the world speaks much of God, it does so only out of habit, and takes its knowledge from the history <term>history</term> <note>original: "Historia." Böhme uses this term to critique a purely intellectual or literal understanding of the Bible that lacks personal spiritual experience.</note> of the literal word, and there is no true knowledge among them: For no one knows the Father except the Son, and he to whom the Son chooses to reveal Him.

7. Therefore we have no true science <term>science</term> <note>original: "Wissenschaft." In the 17th century, this referred to a deep, certain, and systematic knowledge, rather than modern laboratory science.</note> of God unless it be given to us by the Son, who lives in us, provided that we are also branches on the grapevine.

8. For Christ spoke: "He who is of God hears God’s word"; and to the scholars of reason <term>scholars of reason</term> <note>original: "Vernunfts-Gelehrten." This is Böhme’s frequent term for theologians who rely on human logic and academic training rather than divine inspiration.</note>, who were taught only from the letter alone: "Therefore you do not hear, because you are not of God." John 8:47. Likewise <note>original: "Item." A Latin term used to introduce a new item in a list or a similar point.</note>: "You are not my sheep, you are ravening wolves and hirelings."

9. Therefore I say: if we wish to speak rightly of God and understand His will, His words must remain in us in a living effect. For Christ spoke: "Without me you can do nothing"; John 15:5. Likewise: "No one can call God a Lord without the Holy Spirit in him."

<summary>Böhme uses the metaphor of the Tree of Life to describe the spiritual union between believers and Christ, asserting that true knowledge of God comes only through inner revelation. # From the Book of the Threefold Life of Man, Chap. 7, §. 15.
## How we must seek again that which was lost, etc.

### Summaries.

Christ is not found in conflict nor in wise reason. §. 11. It must be nothing but earnestness; heaven must burst open, and hell must tremble. 12. 11. The new birth and the noble stone <note>original: "edlen Stein." Böhme uses alchemical imagery; the "noble stone" refers to the Philosopher's Stone, here representing Christ or the transformed spiritual essence within the soul.</note> are not found in strife, nor in any clever reasoning: You must let go of everything that is in this world, however high-shining it may be, and go into yourself, and simply gather all your sins in which you are captured into one heap, and cast them into the mercy of God, and flee to God and ask Him for forgiveness and for the enlightenment of His Spirit.

12. Do not dispute for long; only be earnest <term>earnestness</term> <note>original: "Ernst." In Böhme's vocabulary, this signifies a total, sincere, and unwavering commitment of the will to the spiritual path.</note>: for then heaven must burst open and hell tremble, and so it happens. You must set all your senses with your reason, and everything that comes in your way, into this: that you will not let go of Him unless He blesses you, just as Jacob wrestled with God the whole night. Even if your conscience says a loud "No," and that God does not want you, you must say: "But I want Him; I will not leave you, even if I am carried to my grave; let my will be Your will; I want what You, Lord, want." And even if all the devils stood around you and said, "desist, it is enough for now," you must say: "No, my mind and will shall not come out of God; it shall be eternally in God; His love is greater than all my sins. If you devils and the world have my mortal body in your prison, I have my Savior and Rebirth-Giver in my soul; He will give me a heavenly body that remains eternally."

13. Just try it in this way, and you will experience wonders; you will soon receive one within you who will help you wrestle, fight, and pray. And even if you cannot speak many words, that does not matter, even if you could only manage that single word of the tax collector: *O God, be merciful to me, a sinner!* <note>A reference to the humble prayer of the Publican in the parable found in Luke 18:13.</note> But when your will, with all reason and senses, is set in God—to not let go of Him even if body and soul should burst—then you hold onto God and break through death and hell and heaven, and you enter into the Temple of Jesus Christ, despite the resistance of all devils. God’s wrath cannot hold you, however great and powerful it may be within you; and though body and soul were burning in wrath and stood in the midst of hell among all the devils, you still tear yourself out and come into the Temple of Christ, where you receive the little wreath of pearls, set with the

noble and most venerable stone, the corner Philosopher’s Stone <note>original: "Lapide Philosophorum angulari." Böhme blends alchemy with scripture here, identifying the "Philosopher's Stone"—the goal of alchemical transformation—with Christ, the biblical "cornerstone."</note>.

14. But know that the Kingdom of Heaven is sown within you in this way, and is as small as a mustard seed: you will surely receive great joy from the angelic crown <note>original: "Engliſchen Kranze." In Böhme’s time, "englisch" usually referred to "angelic" (from *Engel*) rather than the English nation.</note>; but take care, do not place it upon the old Adam <term>old Adam</term> <note>A theological term for the fallen, sinful nature of humanity that must be "put off" to make way for the "new man" in Christ.</note>, or it will go with you as it did with Adam.
->Hold fast to what you have,<-
->To suffer want is an evil guest.<-

15. From a small twig a tree finally grows, if it remains standing in good soil; many a cold, rough wind rustles over a twig until a tree grows from it. It is constant; you must face the Tree of Temptation, as well as the deserts of the world's mockery; if you do not hold fast, you have nothing: if you uproot your twig, you do as Adam did; you will find it harder to replace it than at first. Yet it grows in the Valley of Roses <note>original: "Roſen-Thal." A mystical location representing the inner spiritual paradise or the heart where the soul meets the divine.</note>, hidden from the old Adam. For there was a long time from Adam until Christ’s humanity (during which the Pearl-Tree <note>original: "Perlen-Baum." Another of Böhme's metaphors for the growing divine life within the soul.</note> grew hidden under the veil of Moses <note>original: "Decke Moſis." A reference to 2 Corinthians 3, suggesting that spiritual truth was present but obscured or "veiled" in the Old Testament era.</note>) and yet it came forth in its own time as a tree with beautiful fruit.

16. Therefore, even if you have fallen and lost the beautiful crown, do not despair: seek, knock, come back, and do as you did at first; thus you will experience from what spirit this hand has written; afterward you will receive a tree instead of a twig, and you will say: "Has not my twig become a tree while I slept!" Then for the first time you will know the Philosopher’s Stone; take note of this!
